items.body:
Wickes has officially opened its new store in Harrogate today (21st October), bringing its extensive range of home improvement products, expert advice and design services to local homeowners and trade professionals. The new store was officially opened by Harrogate Councillor Viv Poskit, marking the latest step in the retailer’s continued investment in its store network. The new store will be supported by a team of 21 colleagues, including 19 external hires, creating new employment opportunities in the local area.
Located on Ripon Road, Harrogate (HG1 2BS), the new store features 10,835 sq. ft. of ground floor space, alongside a 3,200 sq. ft. mezzanine housing a dedicated Kitchen and Bathroom showroom. Harrogate introduces a new small store format concept for Wickes, bringing together home improvement products, expert advice and inspiration under one roof. Digital screens throughout the store showcase Wickes’ products and services, helping customers explore ideas for projects of all sizes, from refreshing a room to planning a complete kitchen or bathroom transformation.
The Kitchen and Bathroom showroom allows customers to explore a range of designs and finishes, with Wickes’ Design Consultants on hand to provide the free Kitchen and Bathroom design service and help customers plan with confidence. Customers can also benefit from Wickes’ trusted installation service, alongside 15-minute Click & Collect and the Rapid Delivery service, which offers local orders delivered directly to customers’ doors within three hours, seven days a week, for an additional £6 delivery fee.
The new store features 100 rooftop solar panels, with a combined capacity of 30kW. Expected to generate approximately 41,880kWh of renewable electricity each year, the system supports Wickes’ ongoing investment in more sustainable stores by helping to reduce reliance on grid electricity and associated costs and carbon emissions.
Local trade people can stock up on project essentials, including timber, power tools and cement from trusted brands such as Bosch, Blue Circle and Knauf. TradePro members can save 10% on every purchase, alongside exclusive perks, fuel savings and ongoing rewards.
To celebrate the opening, customers can enjoy 15% off in store from Friday 30th October to Sunday 1st November. Wickes will also host a special decorating event in partnership with Dulux on Saturday 31st October. Customers will have the chance to meet the iconic Dulux dog, take a photo with the much-loved mascot and enter a competition to win Dulux merchandise, while picking up inspiration for their next decorating project.
Kate Thompson, head of property at Wickes, said: “We’re delighted to open our new store in Harrogate, bringing trusted home improvement products and expert advice to the local community. Our new small format store has been designed to make the most of the space, with a dedicated Kitchen and Bathroom showroom to help customers find inspiration and plan their projects with confidence. We’re also pleased to welcome 21 colleagues to the team and look forward to supporting local homeowners and trade professionals with their home improvement projects.”
The Wickes Community Programme has launched in Harrogate, supporting local charities and community groups with donated tools and materials to help improve community spaces. As part of the initiative, the new Harrogate store is supporting Mind Harrogate with supplies to create a partitioned corridor, allowing visitors to access the WC facilities without disrupting counselling sessions. This will help protect confidentiality and create a more private environment, enabling the charity to offer more one to one mental health sessions for the local community.

Following today’s release of Carrefour’s figures for the three months ending 30 September 2026; Eleanor Simpson-Gould, senior retail analyst at GlobalData, a leading intelligence and productivity platform, offers her view: “Carrefour delivered another quarter of steady growth in Q3 2026. Group like-for-like (l-f-l) sales rose 2.3%, ahead of the 2.1% achieved in H1 with all […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
Following today’s release of Carrefour’s figures for the three months ending 30 September 2026; Eleanor Simpson-Gould, senior retail analyst at GlobalData, a leading intelligence and productivity platform, offers her view: “Carrefour delivered another quarter of steady growth in Q3 2026. Group like-for-like (l-f-l) sales rose 2.3%, ahead of the 2.1% achieved in H1 with all three core markets of France, Spain, and Brazil contributing positively. However, the escalating social and security situation in France has overshadowed this performance and forced the group to cut its full-year targets, just as it enters the most important trading period of the year. Carrefour now expects operating margin growth of between 0 and 15 basis points (bps), down from 25bps. It has also lowered its 2026 capital expenditure target to €1.6bn from €1.7bn by scaling back investment in France for the rest of the year, underlining how uncertain the final quarter has become. Carrefour’s strategic roadmap remains intact, and its commercial momentum in FY2026 is encouraging. However, the events in France expose the group’s dependence on its domestic market. Disruption from social unrest may persist in the run-up to the presidential election in May 2027, extending the pressure on profitability well beyond the festive period.
“France had been trading well, with l-f-l sales up 1.2% in Q3, a sixth consecutive quarter of growth, and the former Cora and Match stores continued gaining momentum. The disruption in the region has hit a significant number of urban stores, reducing footfall, shortening opening hours due to curfews, and raising security and logistics costs. With France accounting for more than half of group sales in Q3, the multinational has limited scope to offset weakness in other regions. Carrefour’s priority must be the safety of staff and customers, while its growing Drive and home delivery operations should be utilised to capture demand where stores face restrictions. Price investment must also become more targeted to protect margins in the short term. However, Carrefour must tread carefully, as many French households remain financial stretched with fuel prices close to record highs. Pulling back too far on price risks undoing the gains in price perception it has worked to build this year.
“Spain remains Carrefour’s most consistent market, with l-f-l sales up 2.1%, broadly in line with Q2, supported by sustained price leadership and a strong convenience performance. Carrefour should accelerate its convenience rollout, having opened 35 stores in Q3, as Spain’s resilience will be vital in cushioning group profitability while trading in France is disrupted.
“Brazil built on the stabilisation achieved in H1, with l-f-l sales rising 1.4% in Q3. Atacadão led the improvement, with growth of 2.0% up from 0.5% in Q2. This steady acceleration in a cash and carry market amid high interest rates suggests Atacadão is winning share, rather than benefiting from a market recovery. With nine-month l-f-l growth of just 0.4%, Brazil’s recovery is fragile and Carrefour needs to sustain Atacadão’s momentum and expand its Bulnez own-brand range to retain value-seeking shoppers while consumers remain under pressure.”

items.body:
At a time when households are undergoing financial pressure, Back Market is challenging the idea that consumers should have to buy the newest device to access reliable technology.
At the second annual Slow Tech Summit in Paris today, Back Market announced the launch of The Back Market Outlet, a new lower-cost marketplace for smartphones and MacBooks that are fully functional but have visible cosmetic imperfections, offering greater affordability without compromising on quality or buyer protections. The company also introduced Back Bot and Back Check, two new tools designed to improve the quality, transparency and longevity of refurbished devices.
The announcements form part of Back Market’s broader response to a technology market increasingly shaped by rising tech inflation and the constant pressure to upgrade. As new devices are promoted around incremental improvements and increasingly expensive gimmicky features, consumers are often being asked to spend more, even when existing tech still works.
Back Market’s position is simple. The future of technology should not depend on buying new every year.
The Back Market Outlet: Benefit from lower prices, with the same peace of mind as buying new
Introduced on the main stage by Amandine Durr, chief product officer, Back Market. The Outlet is a new marketplace designed for customers who need reliable technology at the lowest possible price that’s fully functional, but can’t afford to take the risks associated with second-hand peer-to-peer exchanges.
The Outlet, designed to give price-conscious customers an alternative option, offers fully functional refurbished smartphones and MacBooks with visible cosmetic wear. The devices may have scratches and other marks, but the lower prices reflect how they look, not how they perform. Customers will benefit from professional inspection, a one-year warranty, 30 days free returns and Customer Care.
Amandine Durr, CPO, Back Market, comments: “The cost of living is putting pressure on every household, while technology companies continue to raise prices, using the upgrade lie to justify another major new purchase. People should not have to choose between having a device they can afford or a device they can trust. The Outlet changes that equation. Customers can accept cosmetic wear without compromising on performance, and still receive the protection and support they expect from a trusted technology platform.
The Outlet will initially launch as a proof of concept in France and the United Kingdom, through the Back Market app, with smartphones and MacBooks available at launch. A web experience is planned for later in the year, along with a wider roll-out across core markets.
Back Bot: AI-powered robotics to raise refurbishment standards and accelerate circularity.
Back Market also unveiled Back Bot, an AI-powered inspection machine developed by Apkudo for Back Market, in partnership with Back Market’s Innovation Lab.
It is the only technology designed to assess both the functional and cosmetic condition of smartphones and tablets, with support for foldable devices, styluses and headphones to follow. It can support high-volume refurbishment operations, with the capacity to inspect up to 10,000 devices per month.
Through its partnership with Apkudo, Back Market reinforces its commitment to developing solutions that support refurbishers upstream, before devices reach the point of sale. Robotics are central to transforming the refurbishment industry, enabling greater standardisation, transparency, control and quality across the entire refurbishment chain, making refurbished devices a more reliable and sustainable alternative to new.
For consumers, this means higher quality products, fewer returns and greater confidence when buying refurbished.
“Back Market made refurbished easy to buy. Back Bot helps make it easy to trust. A grade backed by consistent measurement, on every device, is how confidence gets built at scale,” Josh Matthews, CEO and co-founder, Apkudo
Back Check: professional diagnostics built for Mac refurbishment
Designed by Back Market Innovation Labs, Back Check is specifically built for professional diagnostic refurbishment workflows, using native macOS software.
With the aim of boosting seller performance on quality checks, Back Check will help test devices faster, identify issues that manual testing can miss, and make more accurate functionality testing and pricing decisions. Its capabilities include cell-level battery diagnostics, thermal stress testing, component tracking and visual defect mapping. The tool is designed to deliver comprehensive testing in approximately 5-10 minutes, compared with manual inspection processes.
Back Check is entering beta with existing suppliers, testing access and pricing models with early users before a broader rollout.
“Slow tech is not about asking people to spend more or settle for less. It is about making better use of the devices already in circulation. With The Outlet, Back Bot and Back Check we are extending that principle across the customer and seller experience: more affordable access, stronger quality process and greater confidence in the refurbished category” Clément Petit, CEO, Back Market
Building confidence across the refurbished tech ecosystem
Together, the three launches represent Back Market’s ambition to make refurbished products more accessible, reliable and transparent. For consumers, The Outlet creates a new way to access functional technology at lower prices whilst retaining the protections associated with a trusted marketplace. For sellers of refurbished products, Back Bot and Back Check provide new tools for standardised testing, identify repair needs, improve grading accuracy and reduce avoidable returns.

HIDE, the ready-to-eat nutrition brand, co-owned by Grace Beverley and backed by Scientific Ambassador Dr Rupy Aujla, is expanding its range with two new delicious high-protein meals available exclusively in selected Tesco stores from Monday (19th October).
Both HIDE’s Chicken Tikka Masala and Chicken Katsu Curries will give shoppers two conveniently delicious, high-protein options with a nutritious twist on some of Britain’s favourite curries.
Developed by chefs in response to consumer demand for bolder, spicier flavours, these dishes were designed to become consumers’ ‘unguilty pleasure’ this winter.
Both meals deliver 30g of protein and at least 9g of fibre per serving, with protein and fibre sourced all from ingredients you would find in your own kitchen – including chicken breast, legumes, whole grains and vegetables.
Dr Rupy Aujla, Scientific Ambassador and Partner at HIDE, said:
“With the weather getting colder and the days getting shorter, food starts playing a big role in our feelings of comfort and even our happiness. We want warming, satisfying, often bigger meals in the winter to make us feel good. But comfort food doesn’t have to be takeout or ultra-processed snacks.
“Warm spices, whole foods, complex carbs and fibre to make you feel fuller and more satisfied – these things are just as comforting. And with the new meals we developed at HIDE, you can have the perfect balance between a satisfying meal and healthy nutrition”
Comfort meals that are both indulgent and nutritious

This new dish pairs tender chicken in a creamy tomato tikka masala sauce with fragrant brown rice and a side of spinach and butter bean saag.

HIDE’s take on this British favourite combines tender chicken breast and katsu curry sauce with edamame brown rice, miso and tenderstem broccoli.

Staying true to HIDE’s core principles, both recipes are made with whole-food ingredients and contain no added protein powders or isolated fibre ingredients.
Faraz Nagree, founder and CEO of Lean Kitchen Network and Founder of HIDE, commented: “The days are getting shorter; everyone wants more warming and comforting meals. The usual healthy options like salads don’t really fill that need, so we were keen to create some more satisfying, filling alternatives that are still just as healthy.
“That’s where our new Chicken Tikka Masala and Katsu curries come in. Developing these recipes was a direct response to customer demand for more spice and bolder flavours, together with our usual high protein and whole foods approach.”

To support its ambitions in the channel, Ember has also invested in additional dedicated resource focused on wholesale and convenience.

items.title: Halfords shares hit speedbump despite accelerating sales
items.summary: Halfords’ share price recovery is facing a bump in the road after warnings of a softer second half overshadowed a boost in sales.  Shares in the motoring retailer fell as much as eight per cent to 256p on Wednesday morning, putting the brakes on the stock’s gradual recovery in recent months.  Halfords posted seven per [...]
items.body:
Halfords shares hit speedbump despite accelerating sales
Halfords’ share price recovery is facing a bump in the road after warnings of a softer second half overshadowed a boost in sales.
Shares in the motoring retailer fell as much as eight per cent to 256p on Wednesday morning, putting the brakes on the stock’s gradual recovery in recent months.
Halfords posted seven per cent sales growth in the six months to October, telling shareholders the firm is making good progress towards its higher profit goal.
In an unscheduled update in August, the FTSE 250 company upgraded its underlying profit target to between £55m and £65m, which would mark a significant increase from last year’s £45m.
Halfords had said record temperatures during the summer were driving “very strong” sales in its seasonal ranges. Chief executive Henry Birch said on Wednesday that the business “continued to perform positively through the first half”.
Jonathan Pritchard and John Stevenson, analysts at Peel Hunt, praised the group’s “bullish” update, which it said shows the retailer is in a “position of strength”.
Before Wednesday’s sell-off, the company’s share price had nearly doubled since Birch’s appointment in April last year. The stock remains 85 per cent higher in the year to date.
But analysts said the slump was likely caused by the company’s expectation that its profit will be weighted towards the first half of this year.
“The strong [first half] performance combined with accelerated investments in marketing and technology in [the second half] will result in underlying profit before tax being weighted towards [first half],” Halfords told investors.
Halfords shares rocket under new boss
Chris Beauchamp, chief market analyst at trading platform IG, said Wednesday’s “nasty reversal” was an inevitable consequence of the “blistering rally” the group’s shares had enjoyed in recent months.
“Like any sportsperson who has enjoyed a speed boost, Halfords shares now look more than a little tired, with earnings estimates needing to catch-up with a share price that moved into fifth gear over the summer,” he said.
Ben Hunt, an analyst at Panmure Liberum, said the share sell-off was more likely caused by investors hoping to cash in on Halfords’s recent rally than being a direct reaction to the group’s trading update.
Halfords has enjoyed a revival in recent months, as new boss Birch has sought to expand the group’s network of garages and improve its retail offering.

items.body:
Morrisons is serving up a Christmas feast with a twist this year, as its 2026 sandwich selection arrives in stores and online, including the new show-stopping Festive Triple Sandwich.
Packing three courses into one sandwich, the Morrisons Festive Triple Sandwich is crafted to take shoppers from starter to cheeseboard without needing to leave the lunch queue. Kicking off the three course feast is prawn cocktail starter, featuring prawns and Marie Rose sauce with lettuce on oatmeal bread, before moving on to a festive feast of chicken, cranberry chutney and stuffing mayo. The final course brings together Wensleydale and cranberry, real ale chutney and mature cheddar for a cheeseboard-inspired finish, available in store and online from the 16th November.
Joining the Festive Triple Sandwich this year is a selection of new creations, each bringing a fresh twist to seasonal favourites. For those who believe Boxing Day calls for a curry, The Best Boxing Day Curry Wrap takes inspiration from the post-Christmas tradition, combining tikka chicken curry with a Brussels sprout and cranberry slaw mix, all wrapped in a chilli wrap.
The Best Festive Ham Hock Sandwich brings together British ham hock and Farmhouse Cheddar on malted bread, finished with festive chutney and a mustard mayo mix.
The plant-based, vegan-friendly Festive Onion Bhaji Sandwich combines onion bhaji, roasted pickled beetroot, vegan mango chutney, vegan tikka paste, crispy onion, veganaise mint mayo and spinach on oatmeal bread.
Delivering a classic Christmas lunch in a handheld bite, the Festive Baguette is filled with chicken, pigs in blankets, stuffing, cranberry sauce and mayonnaise—freshly prepared daily by the Market Street team using baguettes baked right in the in-store bakery.
And with every bite, you’re doing good too, as Morrisons is donating £50,000 from sales of its Christmas sandwich range to its charity partner, Marie Curie. Together, they’re working to improve end-of-life care in communities across the country, helping more families access the best possible care when they need it the most.
Sarah Mozley, senior food to go buyer at Morrisons, said: “We know shoppers look forward to the arrival of our Christmas sandwiches every year, so we wanted to bring together a selection that combines much-loved seasonal favourites with exciting innovation and good, honest value. From Boxing Day curry in a wrap to three courses packed into one sandwich, there’s plenty to feast on this Christmas.”
The Morrisons Christmas sandwich selection is available in stores and online nationwide from 19th October 2026 until 4th January 2027, with the Festive Triple Sandwich launching on 16th November. All sandwiches are available as part of either the core meal deal at £3.65 with a More Card or the premium meal deal at £5.50, giving customers even more great value.
To view the full Christmas range, please visit Morrisons.com.

items.title: West Country folk know good cider – Asda is looking after its customers with Sandford Orchards
items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. One of the UK’s leading cider makers has praised Asda as “progressive” for stocking its ciders in 13 stores across the South West. Barny Butterfield, founder and chief cider maker at Sandford Orchards, says the retailer is “looking after its customers” by partnering with his Devon-based business. “People in the South West drink more cider […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
One of the UK’s leading cider makers has praised Asda as “progressive” for stocking its ciders in 13 stores across the South West. Barny Butterfield, founder and chief cider maker at Sandford Orchards, says the retailer is “looking after its customers” by partnering with his Devon-based business.
“People in the South West drink more cider per head than anywhere in the UK,” says Barny. “Something like a factor of three to one. We grow the apples, we make the cider, and we drink it.
“West Country folk know what good cider tastes like, they expect a certain standard and want to buy it, so Asda is being very progressive by getting our drinks on their shelves. They’re offering exceptional quality to people who know what that means.”
Sandford Orchards was one of nine suppliers to come on board with Asda earlier this summer across the South West, along with others including Furniss of Cornwall, Keltek Brewery and Cornish Tea & Coffee. A further three businesses extended their ranges as Asda strengthened its support for producers across the region.
With stores stocking four lines from Sandford Orchards – Devon Red, The General, Wilde Cherry and Red Zero – Barny, incoming Chair of the National Association of Cider Makers, says Asda customers from Falmouth and Newquay to Paignton and St Austell are now supporting one of the South West’s most important industries.
“We’ve got a team of 30 in the business, and work with eight core apple farms,” he says. “While some businesses will arrange one-year contracts, when we sign a farm up for production we work to a 25-year contract. We’re essentially companion businesses, partners in the endeavour.
With autumn now well and truly set in, Barny explains that the weeks ahead will be some of the busiest of the year for the Sandford Orchards team as they take on the task of harvesting and pressing around 25 million apples. Hundreds of thousands of these will end up on Asda shelves across the South West as cider.
“At our own orchards, we’ve got 25 tree acres which allows for around 306 trees per acre,” he says. “With support from other farms, we work with around 70 varieties of apple. As the nights start to get cooler, it’s a really magical and important moment in a cider maker’s year. It’s the difference in the night and daytime temperatures that trigger the ripening, and that’s when they fall from the trees.
“We let them fall naturally and gather them from the ground when they’re at their richest flavour concentration – and it’s only when we get the fruit to the mill that we know what each year’s vintage will be like.”
This year, says Barny, who started making cider in 2002, promises to be a good one.
“We’re very excited because the summer was very good for apple growing,” he says. “All those long hours of sunshine bode really well as that tends to mean lots of flavour and sweetness.
“Asda’s support not only for Sandford Orchards, but for the wider industry in the region, is hugely important. It backs produce that starts at orchards surrounding these stores and ends up on shelves as quality cider that locals want. It supports a short supply chain, local farmers, local jobs and crucially, it’s long-term and sustainable.
“Once a cider orchard is planted, it can support four or five generations of farmers and carry on producing for up to 150 years. Orchards are long-term commitments, and support like this is huge boost for a crucial local industry.”
Jonathan Pickard, Asda’s Lead Trading Manager – World Foods, Local & Free From – added: “We’re committed to supporting a strong and vibrant local supply chain, giving customers access to quality produce sourced close to their own communities. In an industry as central to a region as cider-making is to the South West, it’s great to work with a leading supplier like Sandford Orchards.”

This landmark global partnership signals Coles’ commitment to better serving the menopausal woman […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! items.body:
Coles will become the first Australian supermarket to join the GenM Collective and adopt the MTick® a menopause-friendly shopping symbol and certification designed to help customers more easily find products that can support one or more of GenM’s 48 signs of menopause.
This landmark global partnership signals Coles’ commitment to better serving the menopausal woman and making the menopause shopping experience easier, more accessible, and built on trust. Building on the success of GenM’s retail partnerships in the UK and early expansion into Australia, Coles is helping to accelerate the mission by delivering trusted menopause support to Australian shoppers.
Rolling out from early 2027, Coles is set to curate MTick-certified product offerings in-store and online, as well as an online menopause support hub with credible, educational resources. Every product awarded the MTick certification must undergo a rigorous, independent certification process, which assesses each product against a robust set of menopause-friendly criteria to demonstrate how it can help support one or more of the 48 signs of menopause.
To date, over 4,000 products have earned MTick certification, with seven of the largest UK retailers displaying MTick-certified products in dedicated areas, either online or in-store, including Boots, Asda, Tesco, Sainsbury’s, and Ocado. In Australia, TerryWhite Chemmart has joined the global GenM Collective, as well as a number of leading Australian health & beauty brands, including Boost Lab, Hey Sister!, Lifespace, Mineralyte, Murad, Sanofi, and Swisse. Now, Coles joins the 180-strong GenM Collective as the first Australian supermarket.
In Australia alone, there are 4.5 million women experiencing menopause at any given time – yet 87 per cent of women report feeling overlooked and underserved by brands and retailers that they’ve trusted all their lives. GenM’s research also shows that 94 per cent of women want to shop menopause-friendly labelled products, but two-thirds (66 per cent) say they can’t find what they’re looking for.1 United by the MTick, Coles and GenM are redefining the retail shopping experience for menopausal women in Australia.
Anna Croft, chief commercial and sustainability officer at Coles, commented: “Finding products that can help support women through menopause shouldn’t be complicated. With millions of customers shopping with Coles every week, we have an opportunity to make trusted information and menopause-friendly products easier to find as part of the everyday shop.
“By bringing the MTick to Coles, customers will be able to more easily identify certified products across everyday categories, from skincare and personal care to vitamins and oral health.
“We’re proud to be the first Australian supermarket to take this step and to help make women’s health more visible and accessible, both in store and online.”
Heather Jackson, CEO and co-founder of GenM, commented: “When I founded GenM, I had a vision to help women better understand their menopause journey and make it easier to find the information, support, and trusted products they need. By raising awareness of the 48 recognised signs of the menopause and increasing visibility of menopause-friendly, MTick-certified support, we can empower women to make informed choices with confidence. It’s not about curing menopause, but supporting women to live their best experience.
“Coles joining the GenM Collective is a significant milestone, not just for us, but for the 4.5 million menopausal women in Australia. Their commitment shows what’s possible when a leading retailer recognises its role to play in better serving the menopausal woman.
“We’ve had an overwhelmingly positive response from women across the UK, and we’re so thrilled to have the opportunity to bring that same support to Australian women. Having a grocer as large and influential as Coles joining our mission to make menopause support more visible, more accessible and more inclusive than ever before is a dream come true. Together, we’re empowering women everywhere to live their best menopause and to search, source, and shop for menopause-friendly products with confidence.”

items.body:
Homewrecker Pimento Cheese, the UK’s first and only pimento cheese, is expanding its range with the launch of its new Jalapeño flavour, available on Ocado from late October.
Made with fresh grated cheddar, cream cheese and piquanté peppers, perked up with Homewrecker’s secret ingredient, a special spice mix, the new flavour combines the brand’s signature rich, creamy texture with a punch of jalapeño.
A taste of home, made in Britain
Homewrecker was created by Jane Davis, a Savannah, Georgia native now based in Leamington Spa. When she moved to the UK, Jane was surprised to find that the Southern staple she had grown up with was nowhere to be found.
Nine years ago, craving a taste of home, Jane made a batch of pimento cheese in her kitchen and took it to her local pub, The Fox & Vivian, asking the chef to cover her burger with it.
The chef loved it and added it to the menu, where it became a firm favourite. And so, Homewrecker was born.
Since then, Jane has set out to introduce British shoppers to pimento cheese, a cornerstone of Southern American cuisine and fondly known by most Southerners as “the caviar of the South.”
Jane Davis, founder of Homewrecker Pimento Cheese said: “When I first moved to the UK from Savannah, I was shocked that pimento cheese wasn’t a thing, especially since this island LOVES cheese. I was so homesick for it that I started making my own, and nine years later we’ve gone from a tub in my kitchen to the shelves of Ocado. Launching Jalapeño feels like the perfect next chapter. It’s got all the creamy, cheesy goodness of our Original, but with a little kick. With our secret ingredient in the mix, it’s impossible to resist — we told y’all things were getting feistier!”
From kitchen experiment to retail shelves
What started as a homemade recipe has grown into an award-winning British food brand, with Homewrecker now stocked in Ocado, Selfridges and independent food retailers.
The OG Homewrecker picked up a Great Taste Award in 2024 and has been part of multiple collaborations with Honest Burgers, including its Deep South special. It was also used on the Mr P Burger by Smith’s of Bourton, which took 3rd place at the 2025 National Burger Awards.
Meet the new Jalapeño
The new Jalapeño flavour brings a little more attitude to the Homewrecker range. It has the same creamy, cheesy base as the Original, with jalapeño adding a fresh, savoury kick.
It is made to be versatile: scoop it onto crackers, slather it into a toastie or melt it through pasta. Warm it through in the oven or microwave for an indulgent melting dip, spoon it over a baked potato, or simply enjoy it straight from the tub.
Born and raised in the Deep South, Homewrecker is a shameless lil’ firecracker, sure to wreak havoc on your relationship with plain ole cheddar.
The new Jalapeño flavour joins Homewrecker Original on Ocado, giving shoppers the choice between the classic and its newer, punchier sibling – or better yet, buy both!
Homewrecker Pimento Cheese Jalapeño, 200g, £6 RRP, launches on Ocado in early October and is also available from selected stockists including Aubrey Allen and Panzers Deli.

items.title: Blocking Lewisham Shopping Centre proves Zack Polanski’s Greens are the worst force in UK politics
items.summary: Lewisham’s Green council has forced Landsec to pull out of shovel-ready plans to redevelop the shopping centre after objecting that it did not contain enough social homes. This is real-time evidence of the damage socialism does to an economy, says Alys Denby The Greens are the worst extremists in British politics. It’s not only their [...]
items.body:
Blocking Lewisham Shopping Centre proves Zack Polanski’s Greens are the worst force in UK politics
Lewisham’s Green council has forced Landsec to pull out of shovel-ready plans to redevelop the shopping centre after objecting that it did not contain enough social homes. This is real-time evidence of the damage socialism does to an economy, says Alys Denby
The Greens are the worst extremists in British politics.
It’s not only their vile ‘Zionism is racism’ policy and commitment to “a single democratic state throughout historic Palestine” – though this in itself puts the party well beyond the pale. It is a de facto commitment to the destruction of Israel, a position not even taken by the Palestinian Liberation Organization, which remains committed to a two-state solution. So twisted is the logic of these ideologues that one of their number, Ashok Kumar, argued on the BBC that opponents of the motion were themselves antisemitic because they conflate Zionism with Judaism. It is no defence that fewer than one per cent of Green Party members voted for this racist motion when their own structures enable and encourage entryism and their leader didn’t even turn up to vote. For his part, Zack Polanski says he would amend – though not completely reject – this policy because “it is for Israel and Palestine to decide”. That’s pathetic.
But it is at least a comfort that, even if the Greens do get into power in a rainbow coalition of City AM’s nightmares, they will have no influence at all on the Middle East. The same can’t be said of London boroughs unfortunate enough to have Green councils. One of these is Lewisham, where Landsec has this week pulled out of redeveloping one of the capital’s grottiest 1970s shopping centres, citing the Green mayor’s opposition. Liam Shrivastava objected that the plans did not contain enough homes for social rent, so instead of the 300 social homes Landsec was going to build Lewisham will get none.
Work was due to start on the £1.5bn project next year after being approved by the previous Labour council. It was going to feature a music venue, 661 student rooms, 445 co-living spaces, new public spaces and a rooftop meadow as well as 98 social houses and 231 discounted properties for key workers. This is in a borough where 11,284 households are on the waiting list for a home.
No homes instead of new homes
In an email quoted in the Greenwich Wire, the company said: “Recent statements from Lewisham Council also make clear that the administration is not able to support the next phase of land assembly needed to unlock the redevelopment of the shopping centre without a significant increase in affordable housing. This would require a material change to the proposals we originally put forward. This position, combined with the exceptionally difficult economic conditions, mean that we no longer see a sufficiently certain route to delivery and have taken the difficult decision to deprioritise the redevelopment of Lewisham Shopping Centre.”
This is not just a blow for Lewisham but for all of London. Why would any developer go through the expensive and needlessly complex process of securing planning permission when a capricious council can get in the way at the very last minute? London’s biggest housebuilder Berkeley Homes has already said it will no longer invest in new sites following the rejection of its proposals for the Aylesham Centre by Southwark’s Green and Liberal Democrat council. Now it is clear that Greens would rather have no housing than new housing, how many others will follow suit?
There could hardly be a clearer demonstration of the damage that socialism does to an economy. As well as social housing targets that even Sadiq Khan has acknowledged are unviable, the Greens want rent controls, wealth taxes, executive pay caps, renationalisation of major industries and a four-day working week. These ideas have failed everywhere they have been tried. Theirs is not a manifesto but a prescription for poverty.
It should not surprise us that a party so impervious to logic and evidence also finds itself susceptible to the oldest hatred.
Alys Denby is opinion and features editor of City AM

items.body:
Costa Coffee has today (21st October 2026) opened its first-ever store in a Cineworld cinema, marking a major milestone in Costa Coffee’s collaboration with Cineworld and its continued expansion into high-footfall leisure destinations across the UK.
Located at Cineworld Ashton-under-Lyne, the store is the first to open as part of Costa Coffee’s recently announce collaboration with Cineworld, which will see Costa Coffee launch in up to 26 cinema locations nationwide.
Movie-goers can now enjoy Costa Coffee’s full range of handcrafted hot and iced beverages, including its signature Mocha Italia taste, alongside toasties and sweet snacks, whether they’re grabbing a coffee before a film or unwinding afterwards.
Designed with comfort and convenience in mind, the store features Costa Coffee’s modern store design and comfortable seating, creating the perfect place for customers to relax before or after a film.
The new store is home to a team of up to 12 baristas, including colleagues who have transitioned to Costa Coffee as part of the opening, helping to ensure familiar faces continue to serve customers and the local community.
To celebrate the new store opening, Costa Coffee and Cineworld will be bringing a weekend of celebrations to Ashton-under-Lyne on Saturday 24 and Sunday 25 October 2026. Customers can enjoy complimentary Costa Coffee samples throughout the weekend, with a prize wheel on Saturday 24 October offering the chance to win a range of prizes, including Costa Coffee and Cineworld merchandise, gift cards and at-home coffee products.
Andrew Miller, Express and corporate sales director UK&I at Costa Coffee, said: “Today’s opening is a significant milestone as we bring Costa Coffee to Cineworld cinemas for the very first time. We’re delighted to open our first cinema store in Ashton-under-Lyne, giving customers another place to enjoy their favourite handcrafted drinks and food as part of a trip to the cinema. This is just the beginning of an exciting rollout that will bring Costa Coffee to movie-goers in locations across the UK.”
Tim Sparrow, retail director at Cineworld, said: “Our partnership with Costa Coffee marks an exciting new chapter for Cineworld. We pride ourselves on elevating the guest experience, from the moment you walk through the doors to when you sit back and watch the magic unfold on the big screen. The addition of Costa Coffee at Cineworld Ashton-under-Lyne is a continuation of our ongoing commitment to enhancing the cinema-going experience, and we look forward to seeing more Costa Coffee stores roll out across our cinemas in due course.”
The Ashton-under-Lyne opening is the first of many Costa Coffee stores due to launch in Cineworld cinemas, with the next location opening in Broughton Park on the 28th October 2026. Further Costa Coffee stores are scheduled to open in Cineworld cinemas across the UK, including locations in Glasgow, Sheffield and Birmingham.
The Costa Coffee store at Cineworld Ashton-under-Lyne is open from 12pm to 9pm Monday to Friday and 9am to 9.30pm on Saturdays and Sundays.

items.body:
Sensei, the  Portuguese retail intelligence company which transforms physical spaces into Conscious Spaces, today unveils its technology in a new Muffato Go store in Curitiba, Brazil. Developed in partnership with Grupo Muffato, one of Brazil’s leading supermarket groups, the store shows how AI helps retailers see, understand and act on everything happening across their store operations.
While Sensei first became known for its autonomous store technology, the intelligence behind those stores has always been designed to address a broader challenge: giving physical retail the ability and the data to understand and automate its own operations in real time. The new Muffato Go will put that capability into practice, showing how the same underlying technology can improve shelf availability, detect losses, automate checkout, manage fresh products and support online order fulfillment.
Headquartered in Portugal and operating across Europe and Brazil, Sensei has deployed its technology in more than 100 autonomous points of sale, including the world’s largest autonomous store, opened in Leiria, Portugal, in 2025. These environments have provided a demanding real-world setting in which to develop and refine its computer vision and proprietary AI models, built specifically for retail.
“The new Muffato Go shows what AI can already do in a physical store. Shoppers get a faster, simpler way to buy, but that is only the visible part. Our models recognise products and shopper interactions as they happen, and store teams get the right task at the right time. The real value is turning what happens in the store into intelligence that supports the entire business, from the shop floor to the head office. That is what we mean by Conscious Spaces: physical spaces that see, understand and act,” says Vasco Portugal, CEO and co-founder of Sensei.
Combining computer vision, deep learning, neural networks and sensor fusion, Sensei’s technology recognises products and pseudonymized customer interactions, builds virtual shopping baskets and enables customers to complete purchases without scanning items individually, by associating the items to a token that represents the customer at the checkout
“Innovation and the willingness to take bold steps are part of who we are. We are committed to making retail increasingly efficient, and the new generation of MGO reflects that ambition: using technology to enhance the shopping experience. With four years of work together with Sensei, that same technology now gives us a clearer view of how the store operates, from the shelf to the checkout,” says Everton Muffato, Director at Grupo Muffato.
Advances in AI-integrated technology also allow the system to handle variable-weight products, extending the experience to fresh produce and bakery items. Beyond the customer journey, the same intelligence alerts store teams when products need replenishing, helps identify losses in real time, and provides more accurate information to support stock management, store layout and online order preparation.
Over the past years, Sensei has continued to develop its proprietary AI models, improving product recognition, and following hundreds of shopper interactions at the same time. Its technology turns real-time observations into practical insights, helping retailers move beyond monitoring individual events to understanding how their stores operate and where action is needed.
The partnership between Sensei and Grupo Muffato began in 2022, with the Muffato Go concept in Curitiba, Sensei’s first deployment outside Europe. Four years later, Grupo Muffato is turning Muffato Go into a new business model for the group, and the new store, which Muffato describes as the largest autonomous store in Latin America, marks the next step in that evolution.
For Sensei, autonomous checkout is one application of a wider vision for physical retail. Through its proprietary computer vision technology and AI models developed specifically for the sector, the company is building Conscious Spaces: physical environments that can see what is happening, understand how they operate, and act on that knowledge.

The launches come as the two-year-old brand grows from around 50 distribution points at launch in 2024 to more than 900 […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! items.body:
Omega Pressery, the UK’s only avocado-oil-focused brand, is launching on Ocado and entering foodservice through leading wholesalers Vegetarian Express and Classic Fine Foods, marking a significant next step in the growth of the business.
The launches come as the two-year-old brand grows from around 50 distribution points at launch in 2024 to more than 900 today across retail, foodservice and international markets. Revenue has grown tenfold year on year, with the business on track to surpass £1m in annual recurring revenue (ARR) before the end of 2026.
To support its next phase of growth, Omega Pressery has also secured a six-figure investment from seasoned FMCG investor Giles Brook, whose previous investments include Surreal, Vita Coco, Pip & Nut, Bio&Me, Dalston’s and Freja. Brook is joining the business in an advisory position, with the investment set to support further growth across retail, foodservice and international markets, alongside increased marketing, team growth and new product development.
From Ocado baskets, to Oddbox to foodservice
Omega Pressery launched on Ocado this week with two SKUs, with a further two due by the end of the year. The listing adds to its presence in Waitrose, Fortnum & Mason and Planet Organic, while the brand has been consistently the UK’s number-one avocado oil seller on Amazon since April 2026. A partnership with fruit and vegetable subscription service Oddbox has also taken its products directly into more consumers’ homes.
The foodservice launch gives chefs and operators access to Omega Pressery’s versatile range through Vegetarian Express and Classic Fine Foods, including Light Avocado Oil in 1L and 5L formats. With a neutral flavour and 270°C smoke point, Light Avocado Oil is suited to high-heat cooking and frying, while Extra Virgin Avocado Oil offers a high smoke point of 240°C making it versatile for cooking, whilst its subtle flavour allows it to be a suitable option for dressings and finishing.
The launches come as the UK avocado oil category continues to grow. NIQ data shows volume sales increased by 28% between April 2024 and April 2026, while value sales rose by 33%, compared with just 1% growth across other oils. Avocado oil still accounts for less than 1% of the UK oil market, leaving significant headroom for further growth across retail and foodservice.
Internationally, Omega Pressery has secured a presence in Kenyan retail and is preparing to launch on Amazon EU, Ireland as well as Eastern Asia through Singapore.
Investment to build a category, not just a brand
Brook’s investment comes as Omega Pressery looks to capitalise on growing interest in avocado oil while developing a more transparent and traceable supply chain from East Africa.
Giles Brook said: “Omega Pressery is one of the most exciting businesses I’ve seen in recent years, and I’m delighted to be joining Niki and Niheer for the journey ahead. From our very first conversations, I was struck by the clarity of their vision and their entrepreneurial ambition.
They are building a business with genuine purpose and integrity, creating a truly differentiated brand while developing a supply chain that sets a new standard for the avocado category. Omega Pressery has all the ingredients to become a category-defining business.”
Nikita Dawda, co-founder of Omega Pressery, said: “We first met Giles through the Brand Growth Heroes Mini MBA programme and quickly realised how aligned we were on the opportunity to grow Omega Pressery while staying true to our values.
With new listings including Ocado and our launch into foodservice, alongside growing momentum with retailers such as Waitrose, we’re at a pivotal point in the business. We were deliberate about who we wanted alongside us, and Giles’ experience with Vita Coco and the coconut value chain is particularly relevant as we navigate the complexities of building a responsible, fully traceable avocado supply chain from East Africa.
Our ambition is to become the home of all things avocado. By focusing on one value chain, we’re building a stronger, more resilient supply chain alongside a growing pipeline of value-added avocado products. Giles understands what it takes to build a category, not just a brand, and his experience and belief in what we’re building make him an incredibly valuable partner. Ultimately, when retailers think of avocado oil, we want them to think of Omega Pressery.”
Building a more valuable and sustainable avocado supply chain
Omega Pressery works with thousands of smallholder farmers across East Africa, the majority of whom are women, including in Kenya and Uganda, with Tanzania next in its expansion plans.
Working with its pressing partners, the business turned more than 4 million Grade B avocados into oil last year, creating value from fruit that might otherwise have limited commercial value. It pays above-market rates to encourage harvesting when fruit is ready, while by-products are repurposed for uses including animal feed, manure and biofuel briquettes.
Direct relationships with growers, selected pressing facilities close to growing regions and a local team of agronomy, procurement and sourcing specialists help Omega Pressery develop a more traceable and resilient supply chain as it scales.

items.title: FTSE 100 landowner pulls £1.5bn London shopping centre plans in row with Green council
items.summary: A FTSE 100-listed landowner has shelved plans for a £1.5bn shopping centre project in South London after a local Green-run council refused to co-operate with the plans. Property giant Landsec, which owns Lewisham Shopping Centre, said it is “deprioritising” its plans to redevelop the site following a row with the local authority over affordable housing.  [...]
items.body:
FTSE 100 landowner pulls £1.5bn London shopping centre plans in row with Green council
A FTSE 100-listed landowner has shelved plans for a £1.5bn shopping centre project in South London after a local Green-run council refused to co-operate with the plans.
Property giant Landsec, which owns Lewisham Shopping Centre, said it is “deprioritising” its plans to redevelop the site following a row with the local authority over affordable housing.
Lewisham Shopping Centre will join a growing list of stalled regeneration projects in London, as developers warn that rising costs and local opposition are making building in the capital unviable.
Landsec’s plans to build 1,744 flats, student accommodation and a new shopping centre on the 17-acre site were approved by Lewisham Council in October last year.
This decision gave the landowner permission to demolish the existing mall, which has stood since 1977, to make way for tower blocks up to 35 storeys high.
But the project had recently been engulfed by a row over social housing, after it emerged that Landsec would only be able to make 98 homes available for social rent, with another 231 allocated for discount rates or for social workers.
Landsec said it had decided to shelve the project after the Green-run council refused to exercise compulsory purchase powers to speed up delivery of the site unless Landsec offered to provide more affordable housing.
Building becomes ‘increasingly challenging’
The property giant said: “Recent statements from Lewisham Council also make clear that the administration is not able to support the next phase of land assembly needed to unlock delivery without a significant increase in affordable housing.
“This would require material changes to the masterplan resulting in substantial delays to the programme.”
Landsec said it is “no secret” that higher interest rates, rising construction costs and complex red tape are tying the hands of London’s builders, making big projects “increasingly challenging”.
“This position, combined with the exceptionally challenging economic conditions, mean that we no longer see a sufficiently certain route to delivery and have taken the difficult decision to de-prioritise the redevelopment of Lewisham Shopping Centre to focus on other residential projects,” the firm added.
Landsec’s decision to stall the project was welcomed by some campaign groups, including the Lewisham People’s Assembly, who claimed the redevelopment would have caused “mass displacement”.
Liam Shrivavasta, the Green Party mayor of Lewisham, said: “I know there were many people who were concerned about this development and will welcome this news. I also know there were many other residents who were looking forward to work starting next year.
“The fact is the conditions for such developments are simply not favourable right now.”
Earlier this month, housebuilder Taylor Wimpey said the case for major projects in London has “evaporated” because of onerous red tape and planning objections.
Berkeley, another leading housebuilder, has recently hit out at decisions to block its developments in Peckham and Kingston upon Thames.
Rob Perrins, the firm’s executive chair, said there is a “gulf between positive planning policies and what actually happens when you try to build homes in London. All the policies support housing, but the decisions block it time and time again”.

items.body:
France’s best kept secret, Marie Morin chocolate mousse, lands in 300 M&S stores and has French expats and influencers going wild: “It’s one of the first things I buy when I go home to Paris”.
Forget elaborate dinner-party desserts and hours spent in the kitchen, one of France’s best-loved chocolate mousses has newly arrived in Britain and influencers are already declaring it their new favourite sweet treat.
Marie Morin’s iconic Traditional Chocolate Mousse is now available in 300 Marks & Spencer stores across the UK, giving British shoppers the chance to try the French dessert that has been a firm favourite across the Channel for years. And if the reaction on social media is anything to go by, it could be the latest French food import to cause a stir.
One influencer described the mousse as “quite possibly one of the nicest things I’ve ever had in my mouth… WOW!!”, while another simply called it “my new favourite chocolate mousse.”
For French expat and foodie @frenchfamilyfood, the arrival has been particularly exciting, admitting that the mousse is “one of the first things I buy when I go home to Paris” and saying she was “so thrilled that it’s now available to buy in the UK.”
Meanwhile, @charlottecohencooks praised the indulgent dessert, highlighting its nutritional credentials saying: “These Marie Morin Dark Chocolate mousses are SO good. Also 8g protein per pot?! Don’t mind if I do.”
And it is not just the taste getting attention. Food influencer @frenchfoodielover was won over by the mousse’s glossy appearance, texture and intense chocolate flavour, describing its “shiny finish” as “incredible” and praising its “really intense chocolate taste.”
So, what is all the fuss about? Unlike many supermarket desserts, Marie Morin’s Traditional Chocolate Mousse is made with just three ingredients: pure cocoa butter chocolate, free-range eggs and salted butter. Made in Brittany and served in distinctive glass jars, it has a rich chocolate flavour and smooth, airy texture, with no colouring agents or preservatives. And it seems Brits are increasingly happy to spend a little more on a quality chocolate treat. Recent Mintel research found that 61% of chocolate lovers see premium chocolate as an “affordable luxury”, with shoppers increasingly favouring quality over quantity[1].
David Morin, who leads UK development for Marie Morin, said “Our family has always believed that the best desserts are made with simple, high-quality ingredients and recipes that stay true to tradition. Expanding beyond France has long been an ambition for us, and launching in the UK is an exciting milestone. To secure a listing with Marks & Spencer from the outset is phenomenal. We are delighted that British shoppers can now discover a dessert that has been loved in France for generations.”
With French food continuing to inspire British shoppers, Marie Morin’s arrival could prove to be the latest Gallic import to make the leap from French favourite to British fridge staple. And judging by the early reaction from influencers, the French really may have been keeping this chocolate mousse to themselves for far too long!
Marie Morin Traditional Chocolate Mousse (2 x 100g) is available in selected 300 Marks & Spencer stores across the UK, RRP £4.79.

The 3412 sq ft store represents a substantial investment from the company, showcasing several room settings above and beyond the core bedroom offering […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! items.body:
Sharps has opened a new concept store at Elliott’s Field Shopping Park in Rugby as part of a wider programme of investment in its retail estate, with further locations set to follow.
The 3412 sq ft store represents a substantial investment from the company, showcasing several room settings above and beyond the core bedroom offering that Sharps has been known for. The opening of the store has provided an additional four jobs for the local economy, and plans are afoot that if the new concept store model is successful, a plan will be developed to roll out further stores across the country.
The new format has been developed to strengthen the role of physical retail within Sharps’ wider sales and design model, creating a larger, more design-led environment in which customers can begin planning their space before progressing to the brand’s established in-home design consultation service.
Located alongside other home, furniture and lifestyle retailers at Elliott’s Field, the Rugby store also reflects a deliberate move towards destination retail. The larger footprint gives Sharps greater visibility among customers already shopping for the home, while providing the space needed to showcase its new design services as well as a broader range of fitted solutions beyond the bedroom.
Rather than replacing Sharps’ existing model, where sales and design experts visit customers at home to understand the space, take measurements and develop a tailored solution, the store adds an earlier stage to the journey.
Customers can explore full room schemes, finishes and materials, work through initial ideas with the store’s Studio Designers and create moodboards before those ideas are developed further within their own home.
The format enables Sharps to showcase multiple room solutions within one location, supporting the company’s expansion into spaces including home offices, living areas, boot rooms and other parts of the home where fitted furniture can provide both storage and design benefits.
Paul McClenaghan, CEO of Sharps Furniture Group, said: “Our investment in Rugby is about defining what we need from physical retail as the customer journey continues to evolve.
“The showroom is no longer the only place where people begin researching a purchase, but that does not make the physical environment less important. It means it has to work harder. Customers need to be able to experience the quality of the product, explore different solutions and get meaningful design input when they visit.
“We have a very strong in-home sales and design model and that remains fundamental to the business. What this format allows us to do is strengthen the journey around it. A customer can begin thinking through their space, their style and what they need from it in store, and our experts can then take that thinking into the home and develop a solution around the realities of the individual property.
“The larger footprint also gives us an opportunity to demonstrate the breadth of what Sharps can now offer. We want customers to see us as a fitted furniture business for the whole home, and being able to show those different applications together is an important part of that.
“Rugby gives us a format from which we can learn as we continue to invest in our estate. It is about creating stores that have a clear role within the wider business and making physical retail work harder at every stage of the customer journey.”
The opening forms part of Sharps’ wider retail investment programme, with several further locations planned to follow as the business develops the concept across its estate.

items.title: Toby Carvery’s new frozen range wins over UK consumers, System1 finds

items.body:
Toby Carvery’s move into the frozen food aisle looks set to be a hit with UK consumers, according to new testing from market research company System1 Group.
The restaurant chain’s new 15-product frozen range, which has launched exclusively at Iceland and The Food Warehouse, achieved a strong 4.2-Star rating on System1’s Test Your Innovation. The Star rating measure consumers’ emotional responses and predicts the sales success of new innovations.
The range also achieved a Buy Shares score of 72%, meaning nearly three-quarters of respondents said they would buy shares in the idea. The score places the range among the top 15% of comparable innovations in System1’s database of more than 60,000 tested ideas.
The range also received an Emotion-into-Action™ score of 77, classified as ‘Good’. This metric combines the type and intensity of consumers’ emotional responses, giving greater weight to emotions most likely to translate into action.
Almost two-thirds (63%) of consumers expressed a positive emotional response, comprising happiness (52%) and surprise (11%). By contrast, just 6% expressed negative emotions. Convenience and variety in particular emerged as spontaneous drivers of happiness, with consumers welcoming the opportunity to enjoy Toby Carvery favourites at home and the breadth of dishes available.
The concept also demonstrated strong brand alignment, with 92% of respondents agreeing that it fitted with the Toby Carvery brand, while 94% considered the range recognisable.
The findings come as restaurant brands increasingly look beyond their traditional dining locations to establish a presence in UK supermarkets. Brands including Pizza Express, Nando’s and Itsu have already expanded into retail, tapping into consumer demand for familiar restaurant experiences at home.
Tristan Findlay, chief growth officer – innovation at System1, commented: “Toby Carvery has done the unexpected, bringing the Sunday roast straight into people’s homes with a ready-to-eat range. It may not be one for me personally, but I’m clearly not speaking for UK consumers, who rated it a strong 4.2 Stars, a sign it’s set to drive trial.
“Hats off to the team: it’s a move nobody saw coming, and the timing is spot on, with hearty British comfort food landing just as the colder months set in. Whether shoppers stick with the freezer aisle or head back to their local carvery will come down to product quality, but in the short term, this one is set to sell.”

items.body:
Asda has today launched Asda Roots – a new apprenticeship programme that gives young people not currently in work or education a permanent job, combined with training and a recognised qualification.
The Asda Roots programme will initially welcome 16 young people into roles across 8 stores, with plans to take on 250 more recruits in 2027. The programme combines permanent paid employment with structured on-the-job learning, allowing participants to earn while they work towards a nationally recognised Level 2 qualification, equivalent to five GCSEs.
Aimed at 18 to 21-year-olds who are not currently in employment, education or training (NEET), Asda Roots will be delivered through the Government’s flagship Foundation Apprenticeship programme and has been developed in partnership with the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) and Inspiro Learning.
The programme forms part of Asda’s wider commitment to creating opportunities for young people and helping more people access meaningful, long-term employment.
James Goodman, chief people officer at Asda, said: ” Too many young people are held back because they haven’t had the opportunity to gain the skills and experience employers look for. Asda Roots aims to break that cycle by combining a permanent job with training, mentoring and a recognised qualification.
We want to give young people the opportunity to earn, learn and develop the skills they need to succeed. Many retail leaders started their careers on the shop floor, and we’re excited to help the next generation take their first step with Asda.”
Minister for Skills, Baroness Jacqui Smith said: “Too often, young people’s futures are shaped by circumstances beyond their control, and we are determined to change that.
“It’s brilliant to see Asda providing new opportunities for young people out of work and education and helping them kickstart their career.
“It comes alongside our reforms to deliver 50,000 more apprenticeships for young people because everyone deserves the chance to earn, learn and build a career, no matter where they start.”
The pilot gave young people referred by the DWP the opportunity to gain valuable workplace experience and take part in a guaranteed interview. Candidates who were not selected for Asda Roots were also considered for seasonal roles where suitable vacancies were available.
Those who demonstrate strong potential will also have opportunities to continue their development through further apprenticeships and career progression across the business.
In addition to workplace experience, apprentices will receive dedicated mentoring, financial literacy training and practical life skills support designed to help them thrive both in and outside of work.
Asda currently supports around 600 apprentices across its business and plans for Asda Roots to become an important pathway for attracting and developing the next generation of retail talent.
The launch builds on Asda’s wider commitment to helping more young people into work. Last month, the retailer announced a significant expansion of its supported internship programme in partnership with DFN Project SEARCH, creating opportunities for more than 200 young people with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) across 35 stores.

items.title: ACS calls on government to support hard-hit forecourts
items.summary: The Association of Convenience Stores (ACS) has called on the chancellor to act in the Budget to support the UK's 8,300+ petrol forecourts, who have been hit hard by higher costs and extremely challenging sales conditions made worse by skyrocketing pump prices. ACS' 2026 Forecourt… This story continues at ACS calls on government to support hard-hit forecourts Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
ACS’ 2026 Forecourt Report has revealed that UK forecourts have less room to invest than last year, with each store spending £14,810 on average compared to £15,550 in 2025.
ACS has warned that investment is being constrained because of major increases in business rates bills for forecourt retailers and the pressure of continued rises in employment costs.
At the till, customer spending is taking a hit due to the sharp rise in fuel prices over the last year, with an average spend of £13.09 compared to £13.48 in 2025 (excluding fuel).
ACS chief executive Ed Woodall said: “It’s easy for the government to point the finger at forecourts when fuel prices go up, but the reality is that they’re exposed to pump price rises themselves.
“When prices at the pump increase, forecourt retailers are losing out because, customers don’t spend as much in store and they rely on those sales to trade viably.”
“Forecourts are crucial national infrastructure and incredibly important to the communities they serve, but have been disproportionately hit by business rates increases, new regulatory reporting requirements and other cost of trading pressures.
“We are calling on the chancellor to take action in the Budget to support both customers and forecourt retailers by freezing fuel duty beyond January 2027, help them to invest by taking pressure off rates bills, and recognise the role they play in providing secure local jobs to over 90,000 people.”
Additional key findings from the Forecourt Report include:
- Forecourts are rated by consumers as one of the top five most essential services in the local community
- 77% of forecourt retailers engaged in some form of community activity over the last year
- 40% of forecourt retailers are now aged 30 or under
- 21% of forecourt retailers took no time off last year
ACS’ #Checkout the Cost of Trading campaign has been running throughout the summer, highlighting the pressure that the convenience sector is under and calling on the government to act. More information on the Cost of Trading campaign hub is here:

items.body:
Getty Images/Maskot
Capita postpones investor event to focus on CSPS fix
Capita has pulled the plug on a planned event for investors, financial analysts and shareholders to prioritise addressing Civil Service Pension Scheme issues
Capita cannot hold an event for shareholders, investors and market watchers because it wants to focus on fixing the botched administration of the Civil Service Pension Scheme (CSPS).
The troubled scheme has already reduced the firm’s profits by £40m.
The outsourcer said its Capital Market Event, planned for 4 November, had been postponed to enable it to “focus on improving the service delivery on the Civil Service Pension Scheme contract”.
It said it will include an update when it announces its trading statement next month. “Alongside its regular trading update in December, Capita will provide a comprehensive update, including detail on the group’s new operational segments following completion of the disposal of the private sector contact centre business,” said a company statement.
It added that it is making good operational progress with the CSPS contract. “This includes the roll-out of new features and further planned upgrades, such as the launch of the retirement modelling tool, which is due to go live in the coming weeks,” it said.
“Capita recognises further improvement in service is required, and we are implementing further automation and strengthening governance, including improved management information.”
Alongside the Cabinet Office, it said it is working on a comprehensive recovery plan, “focusing on improving member experience and delivering operational stability”.
Pension disaster
In 2023, the Cabinet Office awarded Capita a seven-year contract worth £239m for the administration of the CSPS, which has 1.7 million members. The takeover from the previous administrator, MyCSP, took place on 1 December 2025.
Since it took on the contract, Capita has failed to meet its delivery promises, leaving claimants in severe financial difficulties. Thousands of retired civil servants are affected by the CSPS problems – some have waited nearly a year for their pensions, and at least one has been forced to use a food bank.
Capita has admitted it is set to lose money on the contract, with pressure mounting on the organisation, which is heavily reliant on public sector business, due to the government’s current insourcing plans combined with its much-publicised failures.
In January 2026, just a month after Capita took over from MyCSP and following a litany of problems, a troubleshooter stepped in from HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC) to lead an “urgent recovery plan”, which included 150 staff being moved temporarily from HMRC to the service.
Disaster after disaster has now prompted the government to make the decision to bring the service in-house, but no timeline has been given.
A Cabinet Office spokesperson recently told Computer Weekly that the government is “actively shaping a long-term strategy to bring the pension scheme back in-house” – a statement repeated by Cabinet Office minister Sally Jameson.
What is now clear is that the government won’t let Capita flee without fixing a scheme it will inevitably lose. In the debate, Jameson declared her support for the government’s plan for the biggest wave of insourcing in a generation, but made clear that Capita cannot just walk away, leaving a mess.
“I want Capita to pay for their mistakes, not the taxpayers to pay for their mistakes. They don’t get to just walk away and do nothing about it,” she told MPs. “They need to pay for this, they need to get everyone their pensions, and then we’ll look at what needs to be done in terms of the viability of the scheme long term.”
Civil servant campaign groups are demanding the scheme is fixed before the government makes a decision about its future.

items.body:
Ikea stumps up £31.5 million as it looks to make UK fulfilment more efficient and reduce packaging waste
Ikea UK is investing £31.5 million across its Peterborough and Doncaster customer distribution centres (CDC) as the retailer aims to make online fulfilment more efficient and sustainable. In Peterborough, new technology is packaging customer orders to size and reducing material usage by up to 30%, by preventing waste from oversized boxes and filling paper. In Doncaster, Ikea is trialling a new regional fulfilment capability, serving customers in the north and Scotland from a closer location to them.
The investments will strengthen Ikea’s UK fulfilment network as online sales account for 43.3% of total UK sales in financial year 2026. It is investing £30 million in new technology for its Peterborough CDC, with the upgrades taking place over a two-year period. As part of this, it has launched new PackSize technology to prevent waste from oversized cardboard boxes and filling materials by packaging customer orders to size. On average, the technology reduces material usage by up to 30% and void fill by up to 60%.
The technology is expected to increase the share of parcels processed through automation at the Peterborough CDC from 47% today to 75% in 2027, helping the fulfilment team prepare orders for delivery more efficiently. These additional orders would otherwise have been packaged by manually creating a packing carton which includes having to measure the article then creating the cartons to fit the order. Three drones and nests were introduced at the site in January to support inventory management. They scan each aisle in short cycles, helping Ikea to keep stock in the right place and meet customer demand.
Ikea is investing £1.5 million in trialling a new fulfilment capability at its Doncaster CDC. The site now fulfils orders for customers in the Gateshead, Edinburgh and Glasgow areas, with plans for Sheffield to follow. By fulfilling these orders from Doncaster rather than Peterborough, Ikea expects to reduce emissions from delivery journeys by an estimated 280 tonnes of CO2 annually. The new capability has created an additional 80 jobs at the Doncaster site.
David McCabe, CEO and CSO at Ikea UK&IE, says: “We are always on the lookout for new ways to do things better, and that’s true across the operational side of our business just as much as the innovative new products and services we bring to market. These investments in our Peterborough and Doncaster CDCs will ensure fulfilment is smoother than ever and reduce our environmental footprint, while positioning the business for long-term success by strengthening operational efficiency and supporting sustainable growth.”
“Our wonderful teams of co-workers in Peterborough and Doncaster work tirelessly getting orders to our customers, and we couldn’t function without them. We’re empowering our people to get the best out of these new technologies, and we’re excited to watch them grow alongside the business.”
