items.body:
Co-op and Devon & Cornwall Police double retail crime cases solved with new reporting system roll-out
The number of retail crime cases solved has almost doubled during a new crime reporting trial between Co-op and Devon and Cornwall Police in the UK. The partnership, according to those involved, delivers significantly faster justice for offences carried out, with data from Devon & Cornwall Police showing crimes reported through the platform - which is called SentrySIS - achieving a solve rate of almost 60%, which is approaching double the force’s average solve rate for retail crime versus retail crime being reported by those using traditional channels.
Data from Devon & Cornwall Police also revealed that 90% of identified shop theft offenders are repeat offenders, with just 50 individuals responsible for around a quarter of all shop theft offences in the Devon and Cornwall force area, often with more than 100 known offences each. The new system enables stronger intelligence sharing; improved tracking of repeat offenders - connecting multiple offences committed by the same individual and building stronger cases against prolific offenders and, closer collaboration with police both at a local and central level.
Store colleagues upload incident details, CCTV, photos and impact statement enabling police to record and allocate the crime in as little 30 minutes - a process that could take police up to seven days. Furthermore, it removes the need for investigating officers to then approach the retailer for evidence, saving time for retailers and resulting in the average time taken for investigations to be completed and assigned an outcome being slashed by more than a third to 35 days.
The success of the pilot has seen the SentrySIS system, which links to Co-op’s wider partnership working with UK Partners Against Crime (UKPAC), now activated across all Co-op stores in Devon and Cornwall, with discussions now underway with additional police forces. Co-op’s own retail crime levels are falling with the retailer expected to see its lowest levels since the pandemic.
Overall retail crime at Co-op is down almost 20% year-on-year, with incidents of anti-social behaviour and verbal abuse reducing by 35%, along with a double-digit drop in physical assaults. At the same time, however, it remains cautiously optimistic as retail crime levels remain double those levels seen pre-pandemic after the shop crime surge at the start of the decade.
Paul Gerrard, Director - Campaigns, Public Affairs and Policy, Co-op, says: “The reduction in retail crime at Co-op is very welcome, but these are green shoots with crime levels remaining higher than before the pandemic. The success of this initiative demonstrates the benefits that we know can be realised when retailers and police work together. We have seen that offenders can be identified and investigations can progress much faster and, importantly for everyone, outcomes improve significantly. The fact that such a high proportion of crimes are carried out by repeat and prolific offenders highlights why early intervention is so important - every successful investigation has the potential to prevent many future offences from blighting our high streets and local communities.”
Chris Chaloner, Business Crime Sergeant for Devon & Cornwall Police, says: "The results from this pilot have been extremely impressive. The evidence provided through the platform is available to officers immediately, allowing investigations to progress much more quickly. Crucially, this approach helps us to link crimes and identify and target those prolific offenders who are responsible for a disproportionate amount of retail crime. We know that a relatively small number of individuals commit a large volume of offences. By working closely with retailers, building effective partnership and receiving high-quality evidence we can take earlier action, secure more charges and achieve better outcomes for our high streets and communities."
Policing Minister, Sarah Jones, comments: “Collaboration between the retail industry, police and government is exactly what I want to see as Chair of the Retail Crime Forum. This pilot is a great example of what can be achieved when working together to tackle crime. Shop theft is falling across the country, and more criminals are being charged. This is good progress, but we will go further, restoring neighbourhood policing, with thousands more officers already in our communities. We are also changing the law to make it clearer that there will be consequences for shop theft of any value and bringing in a standalone offence for assaulting a retail worker.”
Alastair Woodburn, a Co-op Store Manager in Exeter, says: "The system has fundamentally changed the way we report crime. Our store was one of the first to adopt it. It is quicker to use and gives us confidence that the information police officers need is available to them immediately - and the outcomes are fantastic. Retail crime can be challenging on the frontline, but it is a rewarding job too.”
'“The majority of people rely on and value a local community shop, unfortunately it is just a small number of offenders carrying out most of the crime. This process Identifies and links offenders - building the full picture. Co-op has invested significantly in safety and security measures, and this latest measure sends a loud message to offenders, it clearly shows just how effective it can be when retailers and police work together to tackle the prolific offenders that do so much harm in communities."

items.body:
British bicycle brand Brompton backs BigCommerce as new portal replaces 12-year-old wholesale system
Commerce reports that Brompton, a British foldable bicycle manufacturer, has launched its new partner portal on BigCommerce B2B Edition.
The aim here is to give Brompton’s global network of independent retailers a modern ordering experience, with the portal running on the same BigCommerce instance and product catalogue that powers the company’s direct-to-consumer business.
Brompton first launched its composable direct-to-consumer site on BigCommerce in 2024. The new offering extends that foundation to the wholesale side of the business, which accounts for roughly 75% of Brompton’s total sales across over 1,000 retail partners worldwide.
“Our retail partners are central to Brompton's success. The new Partner Portal gives them a modern, intuitive way to explore our product range, place orders and access the information they need to support our joint customers.” says Oliver Boardman, CTO at Brompton. “This investment is about making it easier for our partners to do business with Brompton and grow alongside us.”
The previous wholesale system was created more than a decade ago and was designed around the company's configurable bicycles. As its range expanded to include electric, titanium and large wheel bikes, the breadth of products, options and content available to partners grew significantly. The new portal provides, according to a press release, “a richer product experience, with clearer imagery, improved product information and curated catalogues that make it easier for partners to understand and access the full Brompton range, while also providing a more scalable foundation for future growth.”
Over time, Brompton plans to increase the range of tools it provides in the system.
“This wasn't just a technology project. It was delivered through close collaboration between teams across Brompton, combining deep knowledge of our products, partners and processes with the technical expertise to bring it all together. AI tools helped accelerate delivery, but the real success came from having engaged people across the business working towards a shared goal,” says Boardman. “That collaboration, combined with the knowledge we've built on the BigCommerce platform, allowed us to launch significantly faster while continuing to build our internal capabilities.”
The portal is live in Germany and Austria, with the remaining European markets and the UK to follow this month. Additional localisation work for the U., Japan, China and Singapore is underway, with full roll-out targeted for completion ahead of the spring.
“Historically we had different systems for different things,” says Boardman. “We want to bring it all together so there’s a single place partners can come to interact with the brand. If we make it as easy as possible for people to work with us, that helps them give our customers a great experience.”
"For years, manufacturers put their digital investment into direct-to-consumer while their dealers made do with ordering tools no shopper would tolerate," says Lance Owide, Vice President of B2B Product Management at Commerce. "That gap is common across manufacturing, but it's closing fast. Brompton deserves credit for recognising the need to serve consumers and partners from one platform, one catalog and one team.”

items.body:
Quail Digital bags a place among Technology Vendor of the Year (UK) finalsts at RTIH Innovation Awards
Retail communications specialist Quail Digital has been named a finalist in the Technology Vendor of the Year (UK) category at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards which celebrate innovation and excellence across the retail technology sector.
The category recognises companies developing innovative technologies that help retailers transform customer experience, improve back-end operations or achieve both.
Quail Digital’s new Pro12 retail headset system incorporates speech recognition and can integrate with AI and connected retail systems which can allow employees to ask questions by voice and receive information through their headsets. This includes checking stock availability without leaving the shop floor to find a colleague or use another device.
The development reflects a wider challenge for retailers as store technology becomes more sophisticated - ensuring that employees can access the information it generates without adding complexity to their working day.
More than 3,000 Quail Digital Pro12 headsets are now in use across more than 500 SPAR stores in the UK and Ireland, demonstrating the technology’s practical application in busy retail environments. The scale of the deployment has also led to the company being appointed as a preferred supplier to SPAR International.
The headsets can also be used to communicate emergency alerts, allowing colleagues to notify one another when assistance is required. This is particularly relevant in convenience retail, where employees may have to manage customer service and security concerns simultaneously.
Tom Downes, CEO at Quail Digital, says: “We’re pleased to be recognised by the RTIH Innovation Awards. As more technology is introduced into stores, retailers also need to consider how employees interact with it. Giving frontline teams easier access to information, without taking them away from customers or adding extra steps to their work, will be an important part of making connected retail systems useful in practice.”

items.body:
Live commerce specialist Whatnot is doubling Irish workforce as It opens doors to new Dublin office
Whatnot, a live commerce platform operating in North America, the UK and Europe, has opened its new European headquarters in Dublin, announcing plans to double its Irish workforce over the next 18 months and open its platform to Irish small businesses in 2027. The company currently employs more than 130 people across the country and is hiring across engineering and AI, operations, strategy, and trust and safety.
“The depth of engineering and AI talent coming out of Ireland’s universities is a big part of why we keep growing the team here,” says Grant LaFontaine, Co-founder and CEO at Whatnot. “Sellers around the world rely on what our Dublin engineers build every day to grow their businesses, and there’s a lot more to build. We’re also opening the platform to small businesses in Ireland next year, so local shops and entrepreneurs can reach the people already shopping on Whatnot in Ireland and around the world, who will then be able to discover the creativity and talent of Irish businesses and entrepreneurs.”
Minister of State Alan Dillon, Department of Enterprise, Tourism and Employment says: “I warmly welcome Whatnot’s decision to establish its new European headquarters in Dublin and to significantly expand its Irish workforce over the coming months. The company’s plan to double its team in Ireland, creating high-quality jobs across engineering, AI, operations, and trust and safety, is a strong endorsement of the exceptional talent available here and of Ireland’s attractiveness as a location for innovation. I wish the Whatnot team every success as they grow their presence in Ireland’s thriving tech ecosystem.”
Mary Buckley, Executive Director at IDA Ireland comments: “Whatnot’s decision to expand its Dublin team demonstrates strong confidence in Ireland’s technology ecosystem and skilled workforce. The new roles in engineering, AI, trust and risk and customer experience highlights the strategic activity being undertaken in Ireland and supports our strategy to attract investments in innovation and digital technologies. IDA Ireland is delighted to partner with Whatnot in this next stage of growth.”

items.body:
SPAR International and Footprints AI come together to increase consumer connections via new platform
Footprints AI and SPAR International have announced a partnership to develop a media marketplace that supports independently operated food retail. The platform would be available to all SPAR licensees, enabling SPAR country organisations to access a single platform to plan, buy, optimise, and measure retail media campaigns, with the same simplicity, precision, and sales tracking as digital advertising.
Footprints AI’s software sits on top of SPAR country organisations’ existing physical and digital retail infrastructure (stores, screens, instore radio, e-commerce, mobile apps, and PoS data) and connects it into one advertiser facing marketplace, while ensuring each organisation keeps full control of its own data, assets, and commercial model.
“Retail media has reached a point where brands and agencies no longer need an isolated network. They need a marketplace that can scale outcomes. The first phase of retail media was about individual retailers monetising their own assets. The next phase is global marketplace infrastructure: advertisers get a more consistent way to plan, buy, optimise, and measure retail media across markets, while local retailers keep control of their data, assets, and commercial model. That is the shift we are building with SPAR,” says Dan Marc, CEO, Footprints AI.
“Retail media is an important growth platform in modern retail. At SPAR our ambition is to connect the strength of our global SPAR network with the power of local retail entrepreneurship, creating a scalable platform that delivers value for customers, retailers and brand partners alike. By combining our vast physical presence, shopper relationships and data capabilities with advanced retail media technology, we are evolving our network into a connected commercial ecosystem that enables brands to engage consumers more effectively across markets while generating new revenue opportunities for SPAR country organisations,” says Tobias Wasmuht, CEO, SPAR International.

items.title: Warehouse tax ‘dropped over fears of Trump trade war’
items.summary: Andy Burnham’s plans for a so-called ‘warehouse tax’ were dropped over fears a raid on US firms like Amazon could spark a trade war with Donald Trump, a top industry body has claimed. The Prime Minister, during his campaign to become Makerfield MP, pledged to hike business rates on “out of town” warehouses to fund [...]
items.body:
Warehouse tax ‘dropped over fears of Trump trade war’
Andy Burnham’s plans for a so-called ‘warehouse tax’ were dropped over fears a raid on US firms like Amazon could spark a trade war with Donald Trump, a top industry body has claimed.
The Prime Minister, during his campaign to become Makerfield MP, pledged to hike business rates on “out of town” warehouses to fund cuts for high street shops, but the Chancellor has since ruled out the plans.
The boss of a top hospitality industry body has now claimed ministers backed down on the plans over fears it could trigger the ire of US President Donald Trump.
Allen Simpson, chief executive of UKHospitality, told City AM: “We have been told the problem is that the big online giants are American, and the White House will look very badly on any tax rise, which hits, say, Amazon.
“That’s not contested. That’s just what the officials say. The problem is: we can’t fix business rates without taxing the big American online giants, and we don’t want to do that because it will start a trade war with Trump.”
The hospitality industry has been attempting to convince the government that high street businesses like pubs pay an unfair share of business rates, compared to online giants like Amazon and Ebay.
Though business rates are currently based on the value of a company’s property, Simpson claims the system should be reformed to, for example, determine a firm’s bill as a percentage of its revenue.
“The problem is that if you make it a percentage of revenue, so [that] an Amazon warehouse is paying as much as a hotel, you have to dramatically increase the business rates on Amazon warehouses,” he said.
Retail bosses against warehouse tax
Simpson said he had been told by officials in Keir Starmer’s governments that they were avoiding a warehouse tax to dodge a trade war with Trump, adding that he believes Healey’s decision to rule out the tax was based on the same calculation.
A Treasury spokesperson said: “As has always been the case, decisions on tax are a matter for the Chancellor to set out at fiscal events, and we do not routinely comment on rumour, speculation or proposals.”
The US President has threatened a trade war in response to UK tax hikes in the past, when he vowed to impose 100 per cent tariffs in response to a digital services tax on American tech firms.
A potential warehouse tax had been staunchly opposed by retail bosses. They claimed that the measure would push up tax on sites used by retailers for storage and distribution, inevitably forcing price rises for shoppers.
Jason Tarry, the chair of John Lewis and Waitrose, had said the tax raid would “reveal a fundamental misunderstanding of how modern high streets work”.
The government says it is taking other measures to support hospitality firms. In July, Burnham announced a 20 per cent business rates cut for pubs.
Speaking at a UKHospitality event on Tuesday, business minister Kate Dearden told sector bosses the government will help deliver “more investment, more jobs, more opportunities, and stronger high streets, and the sustainable growth that reaches every single part of this country”.

items.title: Co-op and police double retail crime cases solved with new system
items.summary: New data has revealed that the number of retail crime cases solved has almost doubled during a new crime reporting trial between Co-op and Devon and Cornwall Police. Data from Devon & Cornwall Police show crimes reported through the platform - which is called SentrySIS… This story continues at Co-op and police double retail crime cases solved with new system Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
Data from Devon & Cornwall Police show crimes reported through the platform – which is called SentrySIS – is achieving a solve rate of almost 60%, approaching double the force’s average solve rate for shop theft reported through traditional channels.
New data also revealed that 90% of identified shop theft offenders are repeat offenders, with just 50 individuals responsible for around a quarter of all shop theft offences in the Devon and Cornwall force area, often with more than 100 known offences each – highlighting the benefits of early intervention to prevent further offences blighting local communities.
The new system enables stronger intelligence sharing; improved tracking of repeat offenders – connecting multiple offences committed by the same individual and building stronger cases against prolific offenders and, closer collaboration with police both at a local and central level.
Store colleagues upload incident details, CCTV, photos and impact statement enabling police to record and allocate the crime in as little 30 minutes – a process that could take police up to seven days.
Furthermore, it removes the need for investigating officers to then approach the retailer for evidence, saving time for retailers and resulting in the average time taken for investigations to be completed and assigned an outcome being slashed by more than a third to just 35 days.
The success of the pilot has seen the SentrySIS system – which links to Co-op’s wider partnership working with UK Partners Against Crime (UKPAC) – activated across all Co-op stores in Devon and Cornwall, with discussions now underway with additional police forces.
Co-op’s own retail crime levels are falling with the retailer expected to see its lowest levels since the pandemic.
The retailer has long been at the forefront of turning a spotlight on the organised criminality blighting communities.
Overall retail crime at Co-op is down almost 20% year-on-year, incidents of anti-social behaviour and verbal abuse reducing by more than a third (35%), along with a double-digit drop in physical assaults.
However, Co-op said it remains cautiously optimistic as retail crime levels remain double those levels seen pre-pandemic after the shop crime surge at the start of the decade.
It added that continued co-operation amongst retailers, police and government is needed to bring about meaningful, sustained and lasting change to tackling retail crime, and its underlying causes.
Paul Gerrard, director – campaigns, public affairs and policy, Co-op, said: “The reduction in retail crime at Co-op is very welcome, but these are green shoots with crime levels remaining higher than before the pandemic.
“The success of this initiative demonstrates the benefits that we know can be realised when retailers and police work together. We have seen that offenders can be identified and investigations can progress much faster and, importantly for everyone, outcomes improve significantly.
“The fact that such a high proportion of crimes are carried out by repeat and prolific offenders highlights why early intervention is so important – every successful investigation has the potential to prevent many future offences from blighting our high streets and local communities.”
Chris Chaloner, business crime sergeant for Devon & Cornwall Police, said: “The results from this pilot have been extremely impressive. The evidence provided through the platform is available to officers immediately, allowing investigations to progress much more quickly.
“Crucially, this approach helps us to link crimes and identify and target prolific those offenders who are responsible for a disproportionate amount of retail crime. We know that a relatively small number of individuals commit a large volume of offences.
“By working closely with retailers, building effective partnership and receiving high-quality evidence we can take earlier action, secure more charges and achieve better outcomes for our high streets and communities.”
Alastair Woodburn, a Co-op store manager in Exeter, said: “The system has fundamentally changed the way we report crime. Our store was one of the first to adopt it.
“It is quicker to use and gives us confidence that the information police officers need is available to them immediately – and the outcomes are fantastic, giving the whole team greater confidence that something will happen when we report crime. Retail crime can be challenging on the frontline, but it is a rewarding job too.
“The majority of people rely on and value a local community shop, unfortunately it is just a small number of offenders carrying out most of the crime. This process Identifies and links offenders – building the full picture.
“Co-op has invested significantly in safety and security measures, and this latest measure sends a loud message to offenders, it clearly shows just how effective it can be when retailers and police work together to tackle the prolific offenders that do so much harm in communities.”
Policing minister, Sarah Jones, said: “Collaboration between the retail industry, police and government is exactly what I want to see as Chair of the Retail Crime Forum. This pilot is a great example of what can be achieved when working together to tackle crime.
“Shop theft is falling across the country, and more criminals are being charged. This is good progress, but we will go further, restoring neighbourhood policing, with thousands more officers already in our communities.
“We are also changing the law to make it clearer that there will be consequences for shop theft of any value and bringing in a standalone offence for assaulting a retail worker.”

items.title: Trump tariff fears 'deter Labour from a rates shake-up' that would help hotels but hit online giants like Amazon
items.summary: UK Hospitality said the Government has promised support for hotels in the Budget, after having given a business rates discount to pubs earlier this year.
items.body:
Trump tariff fears 'deter Labour from a rates shake-up' that would help hotels but hit online giants like Amazon
Labour shelved a business rates shake-up that could have helped hotels but hit online giants such as Amazon because of fears of upsetting Donald Trump, it was claimed yesterday.
Industry group UK Hospitality said that Andy Burnham's government has promised support for hotels in the Budget, after giving a business rates discount to pubs earlier this year.
But chairman Allen Simpson told reporters yesterday: 'We've been told consistently by the Treasury and by officials that one of the reasons they're so wary of doing something on business rates is because to pay for it they'll have to put up taxes on Amazon warehouses, and they think that Trump will hit us with a tariff – so that might be technically difficult to do.'
UK Hospitality did not suggest that Amazon had been lobbying the Government against business rate increases or citing the US President in conversations.
A Treasury spokesman said: 'As has always been the case, decisions on tax are a matter for the Chancellor [John Healey] to set out at fiscal events, and we do not routinely comment on rumour, speculation or proposals.'
Simpson said hotels were facing particularly painful conditions after their business rate bills more than doubled over a three-year period.
Industry group UK Hospitality said that Andy Burnham's Government has promised support for hotels in the Budget, after having given a business rates discount to pubs earlier this year
It has been reported that the Government will introduce business rates reductions for small High Street businesses, such as salons and cafes, by lifting 75,000 small properties out of paying rates.
This is to be funded by a tax crackdown on online retailers that will make them responsible for collecting tax from retailers using their marketplaces. The move has been welcomed by Amazon.
But UK Hospitality has urged ministers to extend support to hotels, many of which face the highest business rates multiplier – part of the formula for calculating rates – because they are large properties.
However, Simpson said that a VAT cut – reducing the rate paid by hospitality from 20 per cent to 10 per cent – was 'the single biggest and simplest lever that they could pull'.
He said the Chancellor expressed sympathy for the sector's plight at a recent roundtable meeting with business, agreeing 'that the last few years have been devastating for the High Street, for hospitality in particular'.

items.body:
CAYO, the luxury Irish alpaca knitwear brand, has officially announced its expansion into the UK retail market with a launch at multi-brand boutique destination Square Bath. Located at 12 New Bond St, Bath, BA1 1BE the collection is located on the ground floor next to Isabel Marant, GANNI, rag & bone, Anine Bing and others. CAYO is also now available to shop online in the UK.
Designed in Ireland and knitted by expert craftspeople in Italy, CAYO garments are engineered for year-round versatility. Founded by Limerick designer Orla Daly, CAYO brings a fresh approach to the luxury knitwear sector with seasonless, heirloom-quality pieces. Unlike fast-fashion knits reliant on synthetic blends, CAYO uses zero synthetic plastic fibers, selecting 100% naturally derived, premium Peruvian alpaca wool custom-spun specifically for the brand.
CAYO was born from founder Orla Daly’s passion for slow fashion and self-expression, which began when her parents gifted her a sewing machine at age 15 and was further shaped by her participation in Junk Couture creating garments from 100% recycled materials. After discovering the unique thermal properties and sustainability of alpaca wool during a trip to South America, Daly set out to create a brand built on transparency and longevity. Alpaca farming requires significantly less land and water resources than cashmere goats or mohair rabbits, offering a gentler footprint on the planet.
Square Bath will stock a curated selection of CAYO’s classic collection alongside the brand’s newly released signature button up cardigan in all new colourways. Every CAYO garment features signature structural design choices and distinctive brand accents:
● The Andean Jumper: A neater, structured silhouette featuring a classic relaxed round neck, tailored split hem and long fitted cuffs. Versatile enough to layer over dresses or pair with denim, it offers temperature-regulating comfort suitable for a cool summer evening or a chilly winter day. Available in Nordic Sky Blue, Sunset Pink. Andean Reimagined is available in: Chantilly Cream, Cream and Ink Blue and Cream and Tan Stripe.
● The Classic Jumper: A relaxed-fit pullover designed for effortless everyday layering and soft, draped comfort. Available in Nordic Sky Blue, Deep Navy, Sunset Pink, Muted Animal Print and Tan.
● The Zip Up Hoodie: A relaxed-fit, longer-line zip knit designed for effortless layering. Crafted in versatile shades like Chantilly Cream (accented with a subtle navy cuff stripe), True Tan, Ink Blue and Sunset Pink, it can be styled under a coat for winter or over dresses on cooler summer evenings.
● The Button Up Cardigan: CAYO’s signature silhouette reimagined with fresh colour mixes and bespoke buttons. Features cloud-like softness and the signature coloured stripe on the right cuff. Available in Burnt Orange and Vibrant Green. The Button Up Cardigan Reimagined is available in Tan with Cream Lapel, Chantilly Cream, True Tan and Cream with Tan Lapel.
● Hats & Scarves: Essential luxury cold weather accessories including The Wrap Around Scarf, an indulgent, oversized knit designed for versatile draped styling and The Peak Hat, crafted with generous depth and shape. Both accessory lines feature CAYO’s distinctive signature contrast stripe along the edge and hem. Hats available in Sunset Pink, Chantilly Cream and Tan. Scarves available in Cream and Tan.
● Signature Detail: Every CAYO piece features the brand’s distinct signature detail: a contrast coloured stripe located on the right cuff of cardigans and jumpers (such as the subtle navy cuff stripe on the Sunset Pink Andean knit) and along the hem edge of hats and scarves.
Orla Daly, CAYO founder, says: “Expanding into the UK market through a premier retailer like Square Bath is such an exciting milestone for CAYO. We set out to create pieces that feel incredible to wear while honouring our commitment to ethical production. By using our custom-spun alpaca yarn, we can offer customers a luxury garment that delivers all the softness of cashmere or mohair, but with far greater durability and easier care. It really is an investment piece designed to be worn and loved season after season.”
The collection is available in-store at Square Bath and online at www.cayo-brand.com / @cayo_the_brand
Pricing ranges from £70-£400.
Square Bath is open Monday-Saturday 10am-6pm and Sunday 10am-5pm. Square Bath: 12 New Bond St, Bath BA1 1BE

items.title: Wickes posts bumper sales but customers put kitchen upgrades on pause as prices rise
items.summary: The DIY retailer said it had seen 'good momentum' in recent months as sales volumes grew as timber, roofing and garden products have boomed.
items.body:
Wickes posts bumper sales but customers put kitchen upgrades on pause as prices rise
Wickes has been boosted by bumper sales even as it warned some customers are pressing pause on bespoke kitchen upgrades as prices start to rise.
The DIY retailer said it had seen ‘good momentum’ in recent months as sales volumes grew as timber, roofing and garden products boomed.
But it said that sales were flat in its design and installation arm as consumer caution hits its bespoke kitchen ranges - which start at around £4,000.
Although there is ‘healthy revenue and volume growth’ in its cheaper ‘lifestyle kitchen’ range of flat-pack ready-to-fit kitchens and bespoke bathrooms, customers are ‘being more considered for larger purchases,’ such as bespoke kitchens.
The London-listed giant also said that ‘mild price inflation’ was starting to filter through ‘after a sustained period of deflation.'
Shares rose 4pc on Tuesday morning after it said total group sales grew 4.5 per cent to £439 million for the three months to 26 September, compared to the same quarter last year.
Kitchen upgrades: Wickes has said customers are pulling pack on pricier home renos
Wickes chief executive David Wood said more customers were choosing the retailer for their home improvement projects. ‘Our continued market share gains demonstrate the strength of our value-led proposition and our ability to outperform in a competitive market,’ he said.
Wickes’ customer reticence over splashing out on pricier kitchens comes after Kingfisher - which owns B&Q and Screwfix - last month said kitchens were doing better than bathrooms.
The retailer said that its summer sales had been hit by a weak demand for its bathroom ranges, while customers forked out on kitchens.
Kingfisher chief executive Thierry Garnier said: ‘People are spending more money on their kitchen today than on their bathroom… a more important part of our lives, it’s becoming a more important room in the house, and we see that across Europe – a more positive trend on kitchen than bathroom.’
AJ Bell investment director Russ Mould said: ‘Where Wickes is faring less well is on the design and installation side where like-for-like revenue was in reverse. This was down to customers being more reluctant to splash out on bespoke kitchens.
‘This is no great shock given the pressure on household finances and Wickes will hope this is spending which might return if or when the backdrop improves.’

“We’re proud to use a product that helps people make fresh, healthy choices every day to support a cause that matters so much. We’re two weeks into the launch and confident we’ll hit out fundraising target for this year. We hope shoppers will join us in getting behind Tickled Pink, and we’d love to see more brands do the same. By working together and finding creative ways to support important causes, we can spread the word and make a real difference.”

items.title: BBC Three and BBC Scotland TV channels to be shut down next year
items.summary: Corporation announces broadcast closures and job losses in effort to find savings of £500m UK politics live – latest updates Television channels BBC Three and BBC Scotland are to close and the Radio 4 Extra radio station will be scrapped, as part of the corporation’s drive to cut £500m in costs. Both TV channels are to move online as executives try to plug a funding crisis and adapt the broadcaster’s output for audiences that increasingly watch content on demand. All three outlets will close in the spring. Continue reading...
items.body:
Television channels BBC Three and BBC Scotland are to close and the Radio 4 Extra radio station will be scrapped, as part of the corporation’s drive to cut £500m in costs.
Both TV channels are to move online as executives try to plug a funding crisis and adapt the broadcaster’s output for audiences that increasingly watch content on demand. All three outlets will close in the spring.
Matt Brittin, the BBC’s director general, said the corporation needed to “make every pound work harder for audiences as we respond to the immediate cost pressures and reinvent the BBC for a changing world”. He added: “We all know that means tough choices.”
A further 100 jobs will also be cut at BBC News to save £5.5m. However, the department’s new director, Rachel Jupp, warned staff that its £51m cuts target could yet increase as a result of the broadcaster’s funding crisis.
Even with the channel closures, which come on top of other cuts already announced, BBC insiders said the corporation was not even half way to meeting its £500m target.
Only about £200m has been cut so far, suggesting even more controversial cuts will have to be made over the next year to plug the funding gap.
It marks the second time that BBC Three’s linear TV channel has been closed, having been moved online in 2016 but brought back in 2022.
The Guardian revealed this month that the channels were likely to be axed.
BBC Three, which is aimed at young audiences, launched shows including Gavin and Stacey, Fleabag and Killing Eve. However, it was an obvious candidate to move online and have more of its content placed on YouTube, where younger audiences have migrated. Typically, about 4% of the UK population watch the channel live in a week.
The BBC promised there would be increased investment in content for younger audiences. It has already cancelled the high-profile BBC Three show RuPaul’s Drag Race UK.
BBC Scotland’s viewership was seen as too low to justify the cost of keeping it on air, with its digital audience increasing via the BBC’s iPlayer. Its content will also be available on BBC One and BBC Two in Scotland.
The decision to close Radio 4 Extra came after it was decided much of its content could be accessed digitally, via the BBC Sounds app. The station reached an audience of 1.4 million a week, according to the most recent Rajar data.
There has already been severe internal criticism from BBC staff over where the cuts are being made.
BBC executives have said they planned to safeguard content that fulfilled its duty to produce programming for everyone. However, many staff now fear that the BBC is targeting public service content that commercial rivals would never replicate.
There has been increasing disquiet over the decision to axe BBC Radio 4’s The World Tonight after more than 50 years. Consumer affairs show You and Yours is one of a number of fellow Radio 4 shows going, to be replaced by a new format.
Some of the BBC’s freelance foreign correspondents have also been cut, while the number of local correspondents across Britain is being reduced, with those still in post asked to become general reporters rather than specialists. Meanwhile, the BBC’s local radio output is being made more regional.
The BBC has also faced a backlash from politicians, as well as from the staff and crew of its flagship radio drama The Archers, after a decision not to build a planned radio drama studio for the show in its new Birmingham headquarters.
The vast majority of staff accept that the corporation is under financial strain and needs to modernise in an age of streaming and digital platforms consumed over a smartphone.
However, morale has been hit by the time it has taken to drip out the cuts, while others believe the cuts will result in the BBC replicating too much content similar to that on commercial networks.
In a note to staff, Brittin said: “We would all prefer immediate certainty. However, it unfortunately takes time to develop proposals that ensure we focus scarcer resources on the shows, stories and services that can have the biggest impact.”
Further major changes to BBC News are still to come, but have been delayed to allow Jupp to draw up her strategy for the newsroom. She has been tasked with boosting BBC News on digital platforms such as YouTube and TikTok, as well as the BBC’s own apps and iPlayer.
Philippa Childs, the head of the Bectu union, said the latest cuts and channel closures were “in danger of causing irreparable damage to the BBC and will do yet more harm to the morale of its employees”.
“The continued drip-feed of planned job and output cuts is putting increasing pressure on an already bruised workforce at the BBC,” she said.
The BBC is having to make the cuts as a result of its serious financial challenges, with its cash revenues falling at an alarming rate over the last year. Brittin has said he was not fully aware of the pressures when he took the job earlier this year.
One BBC insider said the corporation was “taking an axe to so much content that is unmatched by the commercial sector”.
“The pace of this change appears to be accelerating,” they said. “I think there is a very credible threat that there will be an increase in people choosing to opt out of the licence fee because it no longer does them a service. The doom spiral continues.”

items.title: Folkestone and Hythe MP Tony Vaughan meets with Fed national president
items.summary: Kent retailer Hemanshu Patel, who is the national president of the Federation of Independent Retailers (the Fed), met with Folkestone and Hythe MP Tony Vaughan on Friday, 16 October, to discuss current government efforts to tackle the challenge of rogue trade on the high street.… This story continues at Folkestone and Hythe MP Tony Vaughan meets with Fed national president Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
The meeting took place at Patel’s business, Saltwood General Stores, near Hythe, and followed a discussion in December last year.
It also came as the government prepares to introduce new measures that may help law enforcement act on the problem.
The Fed has also raised these issues directly with the government, with Patel speaking with crime and policing minister Sarah Jones at the end of last year and again this week through the Fed’s membership of the Retail Crime Forum.
Patel said: “The Fed represents thousands of responsible independent retailers across the country – as well as the wider independent retail sector – and we back measures the government is taking which will make it more difficult for criminals to trade on the High Street, particularly through closure notices and closure orders.
“Rogue trade funds organised crime, reduces the government’s tax base and is also driving many high street shops out of business.
“Meanwhile, we share the government’s concern about the safety of the goods being sold on the black market which have no quality control.”
Patel and Vaughan also discussed the challenges of retail crime and theft, which is no longer accelerating, but continues to be close to record highs, according to government data.
Patel explained the Fed’s continued concerns around underreporting, along with the legal challenge retailers face when confronting shop keepers, as well as the length of time it can take to report a retail crime offence.
Finally, Patel spoke of the Fed’s work to encourage independent retailers to prepare for the deposit return scheme (DRS) which will launch on 1 October, 2027. He explained the Fed’s was keen to help retailers manage costs and was encouraging members to register.
After the meeting, Tony Vaughan said: “It was very useful to speak to Hemanshu again and to congratulate him on becoming national president of the Fed earlier this year.
He raised some valuable points about rogue trade and retail crime. I am pleased the government is taking this matter seriously, but I will pass on his feedback to government and colleagues in Parliament about how more can be done to tackle the blight of illicit trade.”
Patel added: “I would like to thank Tony for once again visiting my shop and showing his interest in the Federation’s important agenda.
“I said we need to ensure our high streets maintain a balanced mix of businesses that attracts people into our town centres. Vibrant high streets depend on a diverse range of businesses that give people reasons to visit and support their local communities.”

items.title: Commercial property interest up 20% as businesses bet on Britain’s high streets
items.summary: Search interest in commercial properties has increased by 20% year-on-year, according to new analysis of Google search data by Hiscox, suggesting businesses continue to see value in investing in physical premises despite ongoing economic pressures. The findings come at a time when Britain’s high streets… This story continues at Commercial property interest up 20% as businesses bet on Britain’s high streets Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
The findings come at a time when Britain’s high streets are firmly back on the national agenda, with policymakers increasingly focused on how town centres can support local communities and economic growth.
Hiscox analysed year-on-year changes in Google search volumes for terms such as ‘commercial property to rent in [location]’ and ‘commercial property for sale in [location]’, across 1,000 towns and cities in the UK.
The biggest increases in commercial property interest were concentrated in smaller towns and cities, with locations recording triple-digit growth year-on-year:
- Heckmondwike, Yorkshire and the Humber (+635%)
- Devizes, South West (+444%)
- East Kilbride, Scotland (+387%)
- Cumbernauld, Scotland (+320%)
- Northwich, North West (+268%)
- Selby, Yorkshire and the Humber (+265%)
- Barrow-in-Furness, North West (+229%)
- Gainsborough, East Midlands (+224%)
- Bideford, South West (+216%)
- Cwmbran, Wales (+214%)
The data suggests that businesses are casting a wider net when searching for physical premises, looking outside of traditional commercial hubs.
While smaller locations saw the fastest growth rates, interest remains strongest in some of the UK’s biggest cities.
The locations generating the greatest increase in commercial property searches are:
- Manchester, North West (+28,430 searches)
- Bristol, South West (+25,620)
- Edinburgh, Scotland (+25,340)
- Leicester, East Midlands (+25,330)
- Liverpool, North West (+20,580)
- Glasgow, Scotland (+20,130)
- Birmingham, West Midlands (+19,990)
- Sheffield, Yorkshire and the Humber (+19,560)
- Nottingham, East Midlands (+19,390)
- Leeds, Yorkshire and the Humber (+19,050)
Nick Thornhill, direct and partnerships director at Hiscox, commented: “We’re seeing two trends emerge simultaneously. Major cities continue to generate significant levels of commercial property interest, likely because of the scale, talent and connectivity that they offer.
“At the same time, smaller towns are recording some of the fastest rates of growth. They are becoming increasingly attractive destinations for businesses looking to establish or expand a physical presence because they can offer access to local communities, lower costs and new growth opportunities.
“Physical locations continue to offer important advantages for businesses, whether that’s attracting customers, building communities, strengthening brand presence or supporting collaboration among teams.
“The level of interest we’re seeing suggests many businesses continue to view commercial premises as an important investment in long-term growth.”
Hiscox’s research comes as policymakers increasingly focus on the future of Britain’s high streets and how town centres can attract businesses that support local communities and economic growth.
Thornhill said: “The conversation around Britain’s high streets has changed significantly in recent months. Rather than focusing solely on vacancy rates and decline, policymakers are increasingly debating how to encourage businesses that contribute to local communities, attract footfall and create vibrant town centres.
“Our research suggests that there is an appetite among businesses to invest in physical premises, but the economic reality cannot be ignored. For many small businesses, costs such as business rates, rent and utilities remain significant barriers to expansion.
“The government’s decision to provide business rates relief for some high street businesses recognises the pressures that many businesses are under and highlights the importance of physical premises to local economies.”

Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
Following the release of Wickes’ figures for the quarter ending 26 September 2026; Ashley Adeyemi, retail analyst at GlobalData, a leading intelligence and productivity platform, offers her view: “Wickes’ Q3 results offer a rare beacon of hope in an otherwise subdued home improvement market, with group revenue rising 4.5% to £439m, accelerating from 2.3% growth in Q2. Group LFL sales rose 4.0%, driven by a strong recovery in Retail, where LFL growth reached 5.6%, compared to just 0.7% in Q2. This is particularly encouraging given the demanding prior-year comparative of 5.6%, demonstrating Wickes’ resilience amid continued pressure on home improvement spending. Growth remained largely volume-led, with DIY returning to mid-single digit growth as Wickes’ value proposition resonates with cost-conscious consumers.
“TradePro remained a key growth driver, with sales up 8% and active members rising 8% to 684,000. This performance stands out against a subdued construction market, with Travis Perkins reporting a 1.3% LFL sales decline in Q3. While competitors including Travis Perkins and Howdens have raised prices, Wickes’ ambition to remain 2–3% cheaper provides an advantage as tradespeople become more price-sensitive. However, rising input costs will make maintaining this price differential without eroding margins increasingly challenging. Wickes should therefore focus on elevating spend among existing TradePro members through personalised rewards and streamlined repeat purchasing, strengthening customer loyalty and driving growth beyond membership expansion.
“Design & Installation (D&I) offered a less reassuring picture, with LFL revenues declining 0.6%, compared with 1.8% growth in Q2. While Lifestyle Kitchens and Bespoke Bathrooms continued growing, higher-value Bespoke Kitchens remained subdued, with ordered sales declining in value despite project volumes holding flat. This suggests customers are scaling back renovation budgets. More concerningly, D&I revenues reflect orders placed several months earlier, meaning the recent decline in order values could translate into weaker reported sales in subsequent quarters. Wickes’ recently launched Carnaby microshaker kitchen, alongside its new Heritage bathroom collection and statement Wetwall finishes, should help stimulate demand. These design-led ranges give customers a stronger incentive to trade up to premium specifications, helping defend average order values despite caution around larger purchases.
“Investors welcomed the results, with Wickes’ shares climbing by 4.2% in early trading, while the retailer reiterated expectations for around 10% adjusted pre-tax profit growth in 2026. Its expansion strategy remains intact, with five new stores and 12 refits or refreshes planned for the year. The October Paint Event should also support Q4 spending on affordable home refreshes, while continued investment in digital design tools and fulfilment should help convert recovering DIY demand into larger projects by making them easier to plan and complete. However, with inflationary pressures returning, sustaining volume growth without sacrificing margins remains the key test of Wickes’ recovery.”

items.title: New industry event connects convenience sector
items.summary: A new event for the convenience sector took place at the National Railway Museum in York last Thursday (15 October), hosted by specialist convenience insight agency Talysis. Convenience Connected 2026 brought together retailers, brands, suppliers and technology partners from across the convenience ecosystem for a… This story continues at New industry event connects convenience sector Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
Convenience Connected 2026 brought together retailers, brands, suppliers and technology partners from across the convenience ecosystem for a unique day of insight, discussion and collaboration.
With a focus on the future, delegates heard from renowned independent retailer Bobby Singh, followed by Co-op Wholesale (Robbie Moore, trading director), Lindt (Alex Hillhouse, convenience & wholesale controller), Smart Store Network (Jonty Edwards, commercial & operations director, Rascal Systems & Tim Fairs, SG Retail) and PayPoint (Anthony Sappor, banking & digital engagement services director).
Each presentation was followed by a Q&A session, providing further insights into each speaker’s perspective.
Ed Roberts, founder and managing director, Talysis, outlined the factors shaping the future of convenience, the challenges it faces and posing the question “If we were designing the convenience sector from scratch today, what would we build differently and what practical actions should we all begin taking tomorrow?”
The key takeout from Bobby Singh was for all parties to understand and help solve real problems in-store, with a plea for technology in particular that works within his systems and structures.
He also emphasised that everything must either save time, make money or serve the customer better.
Offering a further perspective from retailers, but with a wholesale angle, Robbie Moore stressed that the market needs real growth and shared the six key areas Co-op Wholesale is focused on within its convenience store of the future.
He implored brands to make brand planning more fun for retailers and instore, while stressing the importance of the Gen Z opportunity within convenience.
Having launched Talking Shop earlier this year, Co-op Wholesale’s digital and insight hub for independent retailers, Moore also underlined the importance of making category insights more relevant for the sector, stating that “£500 a week in the till means more to a retailer than an £18 billion category value.”
The brand standpoint was provided by Alex Hillhouse, who demonstrated how Lindt was recognising the potential of convenience and showed the results of addressing the channel’s complexity head on.
He emphasised the importance of putting mission before category to really increase sales and advised brands and service providers to “get more people out to depots” in order to fully understand the sector.
Announcing a new opportunity for the sector, Jonty Edwards & Tim Fairs talked about the retail media revolution and its importance to convenience, whilst unveiling their Smart Store Network initiative.
This social media solution will be launched in November through 200 stores, with thousands more stores coming on board next year.
The final presentation of the day saw Anthony Sappor talk about PayPoint Engage, utilising the technology that’s already in place within 40,000 stores to drive brand activation and generate insights.
The next stage of this initiative will pilot in Q1 next year, offering a shared retailer engagement platform that encompasses support across the supplier base and utilises AI informed by unique convenience data.
Ed Roberts then brought all the speakers together for a final panel discussion, before delegates enjoyed time networking and exploring ideas for further collaboration.
Summing up his experience of the day, Bobby Singh, said: “It was a real pleasure to be involved, representing independent retailers, and I look forward to attending future events. The sector has such huge potential and is delivering amazing results despite all the challenges we’re facing. Just imagine what we could achieve, if we collaborate and work together to level the playing field.”
Ed Roberts, managing director, Talysis, commented: “We’re delighted to have hosted such a fantastic event for the sector and we’ve had the most incredible feedback from delegates.
“We wanted to deliver a thought-provoking, pragmatic discussion with senior stakeholders across the convenience ecosystem and to strengthen the collaborative mindset amongst industry leaders. It’s clear from the comments we’ve received to date that we delivered this and more.
“We’re keen to make this an annual forum and look forward to developing Convenience Connected into a ‘must attend’ event that helps to define the future of convenience.”

items.body:
New Look, one of the UK’s leading fashion brands, has today announced a new charity partnership with Macmillan Cancer Support, bringing together its colleagues and customers to raise vital funds to support people living with cancer across the UK. The multi-year partnership will see the retailer work towards ambitious fundraising targets, mobilising its colleagues and customers across the UK to support Macmillan’s vital work.
The partnership follows a company-wide colleague vote, which saw New Look colleagues select Macmillan Cancer Support as the retailer’s new charity partner. It forms part of the Inclusive Culture pillar of New Look’s Kind to our Core strategy, reflecting its commitment to supporting colleagues, customers and the communities in which it operates.
New Look is encouraging its customers to get behind the cause, with opportunities to donate both online and in-store. As part of the initial rollout, customers will be able to contribute through a dedicated online fundraising page or make a donation at the till when shopping in New Look stores.
The launch marks the beginning of a longer-term fundraising programme, with New Look and Macmillan set to work collaboratively to develop new initiatives and opportunities for colleagues and customers. Building on the initial fundraising activity, the partnership will evolve in its second year and beyond, with both organisations committed to expanding engagement, raising awareness and maximising the impact of their work together.
New Look colleagues have already shown their enthusiasm for the partnership, raising several thousand pounds through fundraising initiatives including a Macmillan bake sale and charity pin badge sales.
For more than 100 years, Macmillan Cancer Support has been doing whatever it takes to support people living with cancer, providing emotional, practical and financial support. The charity also campaigns for better cancer care, helping more people get the best care and support the UK has to offer, whoever and wherever they are.
Lynda Petherick, chief executive officer at New Look, said: “We’re incredibly proud to be partnering with Macmillan Cancer Support, a charity that makes such an important difference to people living with cancer and their loved ones across the UK.
“What makes this partnership particularly special is that it was chosen by our colleagues, who have already shown fantastic enthusiasm and generosity through their fundraising efforts. We’re looking forward to building on this momentum, bringing our customers on board and making a meaningful contribution to Macmillan’s vital work.”
Victoria Floyd, head of corp partnerships at Macmillan Cancer Support said: “We’re delighted to have been chosen as New Look’s charity partner and want to say a huge thank you to everyone who voted for Macmillan. The two-year partnership will help us continue to do whatever it takes for people living with cancer, providing vital emotional, practical and financial support when it’s needed most. We’re really looking forward to building a brilliant partnership together and working with New Look’s colleagues and customers to help more people get the best care and support the UK has to offer, whoever and wherever they are.”
Alongside Macmillan Cancer Support as its national charity partner, New Look continues to support a number of charitable organisations across the UK. Its distribution centre in Stoke on Trent partners with Dougie Mac, its distribution centre in Weymouth partners with Anthony Nolan, while New Look also supports longstanding partner the Retail Trust, which provides wellbeing support and resources to people working in retail.
New Look also works with the Fashion & Textile Children’s Trust, which provides grants to families working in the fashion and textile industry, to combat financial challenges they may be facing. Together, these initiatives form part of New Look’s wider Kind to our Core strategy and its ongoing commitment to supporting the communities connected to its business.

items.title: Smart shoppers make every pound count as the Christmas countdown begins
items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. New research from Mail Metro Media reveals consumers are spending earlier and more strategically this Christmas, with a focus on seeking out the best deals, discounts and loyalty schemes, against a backdrop of economic uncertainty. Findings in Mail Metro Media’s Christmas Countdown 2026 report show British shoppers are preparing for Christmas despite affordability remaining a […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! items.body:
New research from Mail Metro Media reveals consumers are spending earlier and more strategically this Christmas, with a focus on seeking out the best deals, discounts and loyalty schemes, against a backdrop of economic uncertainty.
Findings in Mail Metro Media’s Christmas Countdown 2026 report show British shoppers are preparing for Christmas despite affordability remaining a concern, with 34% worried about being able to afford Christmas, compared with 27% in 2025.
However, rather than cutting back, shoppers are looking for smarter ways to make their budgets go further, with 46% more reliant on retailer loyalty schemes and 29% on deals and discounts this Christmas. Meanwhile, spending is being prioritised in different ways, for example one in three expect to trade up on food and drink, highlighting a willingness to spend where it matters most.
Shoppers are also planning to get a head start, with 27th October marking the start of Christmas gift planning, with shopping getting underway from 1st November. Aligned with the focus on securing a good deal, 58% plan to buy Christmas gifts through Black Friday promotions, while one in two see the event as a way to access products they might otherwise be unable to afford.
For many the physical in-store experience remains irreplaceable. In 2025, half of shoppers found their gift inspirations simply by browsing store aisles, while 78% believe that visiting a store in person creates more lasting memories than digital experiences, and brings the magic of Christmas to life.
Beyond the high street, festive inspiration can also be found online. Social channels continue to play a role in shaping Christmas choices with four in ten consumers using these platforms to inspire their festive shopping decisions, up 10 percentage points since 2024.
AI, too, is changing shopping behaviours with 27% of adults considering using AI for personalised gift recommendations, up from 23% in 2025. This rises to 42% of Gen Z and 41% of Millennials, compared with 17% of Gen X and 8% of Baby Boomers.
Ryan Uhl, Managing Director, Commerce at Mail Metro Media, commented: “The countdown to Christmas really is on. We expect to see a battle of brands going earlier with sales in the run-up to Black Friday, hoping to own a share of squeezed household spend. Knowing that many consumers are keen to shop more strategically, through loyalty and discounts, is valuable both for advertisers and for our planned editorial coverage. Some of the most engaging shopping content we produce helps our readers navigate large sale periods, giving them expertly curated deals and recommended top products.
“For me, the magic of Christmas shopping is being inspired to purchase thoughtful gifts for loved ones, both online and within stores, so I look forward to seeing what brands inspire this year.”

items.title: Gromit Unleashed to open its biggest shop yet, bringing a cracking new experience to Bristol
items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. Wallace & Gromit’s Grand Appeal, the dedicated charity for Bristol Children’s Hospital has announced that a brand-new Gromit Unleashed Shop will open at Cribbs Mall. The new opening will see the store move from its current pop-up space on the top floor of Cribbs Mall into the former Harrods Beauty unit, with a Grand Opening […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! items.body:
Wallace & Gromit’s Grand Appeal, the dedicated charity for Bristol Children’s Hospital has announced that a brand-new Gromit Unleashed Shop will open at Cribbs Mall.
The new opening will see the store move from its current pop-up space on the top floor of Cribbs Mall into the former Harrods Beauty unit, with a Grand Opening set for Friday 23 October.
The move marks the next chapter for Gromit Unleashed at Cribbs Mall and will create a bigger, more interactive destination for visitors to enjoy, with 100 percent of profits supporting The Grand Appeal.
It is a retail model that is strikingly different to that of most charity shops. According to the Charity Retail Association, there are more than 9,900 charity shops across the UK, with new goods accounting for just 8.8 per cent of charity-shop income in April to June 2026. Gromit Unleashed turns the traditional charity-shop model on its head. Rather than selling donated or second-hand goods, its stores are filled entirely with brand-new products designed by The Grand Appeal alongside official Aardman merchandise, with all profits supporting the charity.
The unusual retail model has grown out of the phenomenal success of Gromit Unleashed sculpture trails, created by The Grand Appeal in partnership with Aardman. What began with fans being able to take home miniature figurines of their favourite trail sculptures has grown into extensive collections of gifts, collectables and homeware.
Furthermore, alongside much-loved Gromit Unleashed and Aardman merchandise, the new shop is being designed as an experience in its own right. Visitors can look forward to an interactive store and exhibition space featuring sculpture displays, photo opportunities, creative corners, replicas of Wallace & Gromit’s Moon Rocket and the Motorbike and Sidecar and a shorts cinema celebrating the worlds of Wallace & Gromit, Gromit Unleashed and Aardman.
Anna Hitchcock, head of commercial, The Grand Appeal commented: “We want people to walk through the doors and immediately feel that unmistakable Gromit Unleashed magic.
“Our shops have always been a little different. We create products people genuinely want to own, inspired by the incredible artwork and characters that have captured people’s imaginations through our trails.
“This new shop allows us to take that idea further. It’s bigger, more immersive and somewhere we hope families and fans will want to spend time, whether they’re watching an Aardman short, meeting a familiar sculpture, getting creative or posing for a photo.
“And underneath all the fun is something incredibly important. Every purchase helps us continue supporting Bristol Children’s Hospital and the remarkable children and families cared for there. It means you can come in, have a brilliant time, take home something you love and know that your visit is helping make a difference too.”
The new shop builds on the long-standing partnership between Cribbs Mall and The Grand Appeal, which dates to the first Gromit Unleashed trail in 2013. Since then, Cribbs has supported the charity through retail space, sculpture displays, fundraising and major campaign activity, helping to bring Gromit Unleashed to thousands of visitors and supporters.
In 2025, Cribbs played a pivotal role in Gromit Unleashed 3, providing a prominent retail presence and hosting both the public exhibition and auction at the Gromit Unleashed Pavilion. The campaign raised more than £2 million overall, including £1.6 million at auction, with funds supporting sick children, babies and their families across Bristol, the South West and beyond.
Lizzie Taylor, senior centre manager, Cribbs Mall, said: “Cribbs Mall has been proud to support The Grand Appeal and Gromit Unleashed for many years, and we’re delighted to be part of this exciting next chapter. The new store and exhibition space will bring something truly special to Cribbs Mall, giving visitors even more reasons to come together, explore, take photos and support a cause that means so much to families across Bristol and beyond.”
The store will be officially opened by Wallace & Gromit on Friday 23 October at 11am.
For the opening day and weekend, the first 100 customers each day will be given a golden ticket at the point of purchase to be in with a chance of securing a discount or small Gromit Unleashed gift. Inside a handful of the tickets, that will be picked at random, is a chance to win a signed copy of the new Aardman book, Grand. The Autobiography of Gromit as told to Nick Park.
The opening comes during a milestone year for the charity and its partners. Bristol Children’s Hospital is celebrating 25 years in its purpose-built home, which was officially opened in 2001, with The Grand Appeal raising £12 million of the original £30 million build cost through its first capital appeal. The year also marks Aardman’s 50th anniversary, celebrating five decades of creativity from the Bristol studio behind Wallace & Gromit.
For more information visit www.gromitunleashedshop.org.uk and www.grandappeal.org.uk

To help teachers bring fresh produce into the classroom, the discounter is providing £150,000 worth of digital gift cards throughout the school year. Each worth […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
Lidl GB has today announced a major expansion of its free education programme in schools, offering direct funding to teachers and extending nutritional learning across the entire primary school journey.
To help teachers bring fresh produce into the classroom, the discounter is providing £150,000 worth of digital gift cards throughout the school year. Each worth £100, the vouchers will allow primary school teachers to purchase fresh fruit and vegetables for hands-on tasting sessions.
Initially introduced for Year 1 and Year 2 pupils, the Lidl Foodies programme is also now rolling out new materials for children aged 8 to 11. Teachers will gain free access to ready-to-use, 20-minute lesson plans, interactive classroom activities, and digital guides focusing on three vital new topics: sustainable farming, reducing food waste, and the Planetary Health Diet.
The expansion follows strong adoption of the Lidl Foodies programme, which now features in a quarter of all primary schools in Great Britain and has been backed by over £1 million in Lidl funding to date. To make the materials as accessible as possible for both teachers and parents, Lidl has now launched a dedicated healthy eating hub hosting all free teaching tools and grant application details.
The rollout comes against a backdrop of ongoing challenges in youth food education. Research conducted by Lidl earlier this year1 highlighted widespread confusion among young people, revealing that nearly one in five (19%) children believe tomato ketchup and strawberry milkshakes count toward their five-a-day, while over a fifth (22%) think broccoli is produced in a factory or harvested from a freezer.
Georgina Hall, director of corporate affairs at Lidl GB, said: “Getting children excited about fresh, healthy food starts with practical experience in the classroom. Having already invested more than £1 million to reach a quarter of British primary schools, we know how powerful hands-on learning can be, but we need to do more. By putting £150,000 directly into the hands of teachers for classroom tasting sessions and opening up our resources to older primary pupils, we’re helping schools build positive, lifelong food habits for the next generation.”
Farming and Food Minister Stephen Morgan MP said: “Teaching children to understand where their food comes from and having confidence to make healthy choices is vital for building healthier communities. It’s great to see initiatives like this one helping more children discover and enjoy fresh, nutritious food.”
The expansion supports Lidl GB’s broader target to reach 35% of all British primary schools by July 2027 under its ‘Better Futures’ community commitment.
Teachers and schools can apply for one of the 1,500 fresh food gift cards – worth £100 – and access the free educational resources via the new Lidl Foodies website: http://lidlfoodies.co.uk .

items.title: The psychology of rewards: what makes digital experiences engaging?
items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. In the landscape of digital platforms, engagement is a vital metric. Whether users are browsing e-commerce websites, participating in social media, or exploring interactive digital services, the psychology of rewards plays a decisive role in shaping their experiences. But why do rewards drive engagement so effectively? Understanding the psychological mechanisms behind rewards can help uncover […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! items.body:
In the landscape of digital platforms, engagement is a vital metric. Whether users are browsing e-commerce websites, participating in social media, or exploring interactive digital services, the psychology of rewards plays a decisive role in shaping their experiences. But why do rewards drive engagement so effectively? Understanding the psychological mechanisms behind rewards can help uncover what makes digital experiences not just entertaining but compelling.
Understanding the human reward system
At the heart of digital engagement lies the brain’s reward system. This network of neural pathways motivates individuals to pursue actions that lead to pleasure or satisfaction. When users receive a reward, be it a badge, discount, or a virtual trophy, it can reinforce the desire to repeat a behaviour. In digital settings, these reward mechanisms can be activated by simple actions: sharing a post, reaching a new level, or unlocking exclusive content.
The immediacy and predictability of these rewards strengthen positive associations with the platform. Variable rewards, those that occur at unpredictable intervals, can be especially influential. This principle is used in a variety of environments, from social networks to gaming apps. It also applies to activities such as using an online casino, where outcomes may be uncertain. In these settings, anticipation can influence how people respond to the experience and whether they choose to return.
The role of intrinsic and extrinsic motivation
Rewards in digital environments can be divided into intrinsic and extrinsic types. Intrinsic motivation comes from within; users engage with a platform because they find it enjoyable or fulfilling in itself. For example, someone might log into a language learning app daily because they genuinely enjoy mastering new words and phrases. Extrinsic motivation, on the other hand, relies on external rewards such as points, rankings, or special offers. Both motivations contribute to user engagement, but the most engaging digital experiences often blend these approaches seamlessly, encouraging long-term loyalty and active participation.
Designers and developers use a range of techniques to leverage these motivations. Progress bars, daily challenges, and achievement badges create a sense of accomplishment and progression. When users feel their actions contribute to a larger goal, whether personal or competitive, they are more likely to remain engaged. The key lies in balancing the reward structure to avoid diminishing returns; too many extrinsic rewards can overshadow the enjoyment of the activity itself, reducing overall engagement.
Personalisation and social dynamics
Today’s digital experiences don’t offer rewards in isolation. Personalisation plays a crucial role in making rewards meaningful to individual users. Platforms use data analytics and user behaviour to serve up custom-tailored rewards, aligning with personal preferences or past activity. These personalised touches can range from curated recommendations to exclusive offers, making users feel recognised and valued.
Social dynamics also amplify the impact of digital rewards. Sharing achievements, leaderboards, or progress comparisons tap into a user’s desire for social recognition. Engaging in challenges with friends or publicising milestones enhances motivation, benefitting from friendly competition or community support. These social elements transform individual rewards into shared experiences, increasing engagement across the platform. Importantly, social mechanics must be designed ethically, fostering a positive environment that prioritises user well-being.
Creating habit-forming experiences
Many successful digital platforms incorporate reward systems that turn occasional users into regular participants. Habit formation relies on triggers, actions, rewards, and investment: a cycle that strengthens with each repetition. By providing immediate feedback and consistent rewards, platforms encourage users to build routines around their digital experiences. This might mean checking in for a daily bonus, unlocking new content after a certain action, or reaching new achievement milestones.
However, ethical considerations are essential in developing habit-forming features. Designers should focus on creating authentic value and enjoyment, rather than manipulating users into excessive or harmful usage. Transparent reward systems, clear communication of benefits, and respect for healthy boundaries support responsible engagement. As digital experiences continue to evolve, understanding the psychology of rewards remains vital to crafting engaging, trustworthy, and sustainable platforms.
