items.title: Do we really need clothes delivered in under an hour? Target’s Uber Eats deal is convenience culture gone wild | Maggie Zhou
items.summary: The time lag between ordering a meal and its packaging hitting your rubbish bin is ridiculously brief. Will items bought through this partnership be treated differently? In a move nobody outside of boardrooms asked for, Target has become the first fashion retailer in Australia to make its products available to order via the Uber Eats app as of September. This means that a “curated” selection of 25,000 of Target’s products can arrive at your door in under an hour, thanks to Uber Eats’ “on-demand” delivery. It follows Bunnings’ introduction to the platform in February, and Kmart appears to be following suit with Uber delivery available on some eligible orders. Big W has also joined in on the action, with more than 35,000 Big W “essentials” (their words, not mine) now ready to be delivered to your home in 60 minutes via DoorDash. Sign up for the fun stuff with our rundown of must-reads, pop culture and tips for the weekend, every Sunday morning Continue reading...
items.body:
In a move nobody outside of boardrooms asked for, Target has become the first fashion retailer in Australia to make its products available to order via the Uber Eats app as of September. This means that a “curated” selection of 25,000 of Target’s products can arrive at your door in under an hour, thanks to Uber Eats’ “on-demand” delivery.
It follows Bunnings’ introduction to the platform in February, and Kmart appears to be following suit with Uber delivery available on some eligible orders. Big W has also joined in on the action, with more than 35,000 Big W “essentials” (their words, not mine) now ready to be delivered to your home in 60 minutes via DoorDash.
You can buy women’s heels, fashion jewellery, pyjamas and men’s suits, jocks and Christmas merch. You can buy homewares, baby goods, accessories, toys and beauty products, too. This sits side-by-side with Uber Eats’ main offerings of, well, things you can eat.
Each year, the average Australian buys 56 new clothing items and sends 23kg of textile to waste. Instead of being cherished, passed down and respected, clothes are increasingly seen as disposable. Garments displayed next to your weekly grocery shop or hangover order is the most explicit and unabashed pronouncement of this.
Uber Eats is known for being a platform for perishable items. How much time does it take to scoff down a burger or wipe clean a container of pad thai? The time lag between ordering a meal and having its packaging hit your rubbish bin is ridiculously brief. I wonder whether items bought from Target through Uber Eats will be treated any differently.
Much of its fashion offerings are everyday pieces, such as underwear and activewear, items people most likely have at home already. So why the need for almost instantaneous delivery? Ostensibly because of a lack of planning – perhaps for a last-minute sleepover, swim or hike. What happened to good old-fashioned problem-solving? Turn your knickers inside out, borrow someone else’s bathers, make do with what you’re wearing, be OK with getting a bit clammy.
This Target alliance does a disservice to Uber’s longstanding partnership with Red Cross. For the past eight years, Uber has run a one-day clothing drive with the charity, providing free courier pick-ups for Australians to donate their own pre-loved clothes. Just two hours into this year’s day, an estimated 27,200kg of clothing had already been donated. I picture truckloads of clothing being shuttled between shops and homes, and homes and shops.
I’m not negating the helpfulness of delivery services, particularly for those who might be disabled, time-poor or who live rurally. Online delivery is vital for connecting so many to goods and services they need (though it’s worth noting this service is rolling out from Target’s “high-demand” locations).
The speed of this “on-demand” delivery is what’s worrying for me. How urgent is something you didn’t need until an hour ago? Do you really need a “clear can” storage or “mini terracotta pots” or a “Minecraft Overworld arcade air hockey set” delivered to you by someone carrying only a handful of other orders?
This latest tech retail partnership is a timely reminder of our dependence on convenience. Having whatever we want, wherever and whenever we want, has become a given, with delivery apps at our beck and call. We can have our cake and eat it too (your driver will drop it off in seven minutes).
I’m certain we’re all capable of turning into a little Veruca Salt – that spoiled, vexing kid from Charlie and the Chocolate Factory. Tech companies know we have this squirming, petulant child inside of us and are set on catering to our basest desires: “Daddy, I want another pony!”
We’ve made it so easy to line the pockets of these retail and tech conglomerates; we’re happy to pay their service fees and don’t mind that the delivery window is actually closer to 90 minutes in some regions.
It’s now so easy to buy whatever we want that we keep forgetting to ask ourselves if we actually wanted it in the first place.
- Maggie Zhou is a Melbourne-based writer, fashion sustainability advocate and the co-host of the Culture Club podcast

items.title: How to fight rogue shops | Viewpoint: Jonathan James
items.summary: ‘Hidden in plain sight’ perfectly sums up the illicit trade we are all battling against. I am pleased to see the ACS highlighting the rogue traders that are blatantly trading in a high street near you. It’s soul destroying knowing that the stores we run… This story continues at How to fight rogue shops | Viewpoint: Jonathan James Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
It’s soul destroying knowing that the stores we run are rightfully abiding by the law, paying the correct wages and taxes while adhering to the very latest legislation brought about by yet another knee-jerk reaction from the government.
Yet just a few doors along the high street, rogue traders are doing completely the opposite and thumbing their noses at the authorities. Where such stores are shut down nearby, it’s very noticeable in our increased sales of tobacco and vapes in particular.
I know only too well that volume of rogue traders will make it a mammoth task for police and trading standards to get to them and close them down. Irritatingly, many just shut for a few days and reopen. But legislation is now in place to shut them down for much longer.
Legislation needs to be in place to hold landlords responsible too for permitting rogue traders to operate from their premises. A two-pronged attack will ensure every possible effort is made to prevent dishonourable stores from opening.
On a different topic, we recently held our first-ever supplier day in London. My journey really has been an interesting one – from opening a little farm shop on my father’s smallholding to having some of the biggest brands on the planet wanting to work with my business to grow sales. What it highlighted to me was the importance of NPD and range.
In a world where everyone is chasing the same pound, keeping our stores totally up to date with the very latest products while retaining a key core means we are making sure we remain relevant to our consumers. My business was founded on partnerships, and being an independent retailer is all about that.
Jonathan James is the owner of James Convenience Retail

items.title: Christmas retail sales forecast to hit all time high of £93.76bn
items.summary: Retail sales are forecast to rise a further 2.9% this year, as inflation drives spending to unprecedented levels. The Shopping for Christmas Report, by savings site VoucherCodes.co.uk, reveals UK consumers will spend £93.76bn over the six-week Christmas period (mid-November through end of December) - an extra… This story continues at Christmas retail sales forecast to hit all time high of £93.76bn Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
The Shopping for Christmas Report, by savings site VoucherCodes.co.uk, reveals UK consumers will spend £93.76bn over the six-week Christmas period (mid-November through end of December) – an extra £2.64bn on top of the £91.12bn spent in 2025.
While total retail spending is up, sales volume is expected to fall by a marginal 0.2% year-on-year. This indicates that the value growth is largely driven by inflationary pressures rather than consumers purchasing more items.
Despite dwindling purchase volume, the UK is set to lead European Christmas retail spend. Germany is set to trail behind in second place at £74.78bn, even with its’ larger population size.
Looking closer at where UK consumers are spending this Christmas, groceries (£8.53bn) rank second behind gifting (£11.97bn ), holiday travel (£2.36bn) and decorations (£0.65bn).#
Moji Oshisanya, chief commercial officer at VoucherCodes.co.uk, explained: “Our report shows that while festive spend is set to break records this year, the underlying data tells a less joyful story.
“Consumer budgets are under more stress than ever and after several years of cutting back, Brits are having to prioritise carefully how and where they spend their money to protect their most important Christmas traditions.
“Encouraging consumers to spend is going to be a challenge this year, so retailers will have to use every tool in their arsenal.
“From competitive pricing and discounts, to offering genuine value and a seamless customer experience, consumers need to feel confident that they’re making the right choice when shopping with you.”

items.title: Mulberry turnaround bearing fruit as new bags help sales surge by 18%
items.summary: The group said that its new products did well, including summery raffia and crochet bags and a new leather Stevie bag which costs £1,295. They helped sales rise 10 per cent in the UK.
items.body:
Mulberry turnaround bearing fruit as new bags help sales surge by 18%
Mulberry sales rose 18 per cent over the first half of the year as a turnaround continues to bear fruit.
The British luxury label said it was seeing ‘strong customer demand’ after appetite for new handbags helped sales leap by 28 per cent in the US over the six months to 26 September.
It pointed to further ‘proof points’ of recovery under its ‘Back to the Mulberry Spirit’ strategy, sending shares up 4 per cent on Monday morning.
The group said that its new products did well, including summery raffia and crochet bags and a new leather Stevie bag which costs £1,295. They helped sales rise 10 per cent in the UK.
The brand has been appealing to new customers in Gen Z while existing customers have been returning to buy new bags.
Fans of the brand have been reeled back in by new versions of flagship products such as its Bayswater and Roxanne bag. The latter was first popular in the 2000s and is now fronted by Wicked actress Cynthia Erivo.
Mulberry has been attempting to revive fortunes under a turnaround focusing on its 'it girl' appeal.
It said recent sales have also benefited from ‘heightened brand visibility’ after its new creative director Christopher Kane debuted his fashion ranges at London Fashion Week.
Chief executive Andrea Baldo’s turnaround has focused on reviving the firm’s ‘cool Britannia’ image from the 2010s, when 'It girls' like Alexa Chung - who has a bag named after her - paraded its products.
Since then, the business has struggled to maintain its customers' interest and cut a quarter of its jobs two years ago as sales plummeted.
But shares have more than doubled over the past year as signs of improvement have begun to show.
Baldo said: ‘The strength of our performance reflects the work undertaken over the past year to refocus the Group around product, brand and customer, while maintaining a disciplined approach to trading and cost management.’
‘There remains much more to achieve as part of our strategic plan, and we are operating in a challenging trading environment. However, we enter the second half with a strong product pipeline, increased brand desirability and a clear focus on delivering our strategy.'
Baldo has focused on boosting Mulberry’s UK presence with more concessions in John Lewis and Selfridges stores. It has shut shops in China, which has been hit by a slump in demand for luxury goods over the past few years.
Despite the focus on its home market, demand in the US has been buoyed as the business sells more goods through wholesale and started selling bags on department store Bloomingdale’s marketplace website.
Mulberry said it had also maintained a disciplined approach to trading, resisting discounting and generating strong full-price sales.’
Baldo has been trying to offer consumers value for money by trying to win in the £800-£1,200 price range. He has rejigged prices so that now 60 per cent of the group’s wares are sold below £1,000.
The business flagged a ‘challenging macro environment’ as economic pressures across the world and the war in the Middle East weigh on luxury sentiment.
But it said it had entered the second half with ‘increased customer engagement’ and buzz around new products including three new colours - Delilah, Oxblood and Vintage Oak - for its bags.
The results come ahead of quarterly updates from luxury giants Hermes and Gucci owner Kering this week, which are expected to shed further light on the scale of a sector-wide slump.

items.title: City of London urged against business rates hikes to cover £70m shortfall
items.summary: The City of London Corporation has been warned that hiking business rates to cover its £70m budget shortfall would undermine the Square Mile’s global “competitiveness”.  The local authority is weighing up whether to increase the business rates multiplier it charges businesses in the Square Mile, but a member of its finance committee has warned that [...]
items.body:
City of London urged against business rates hikes to cover £70m shortfall
The City of London Corporation has been warned that hiking business rates to cover its £70m budget shortfall would undermine the Square Mile’s global “competitiveness”.
The local authority is weighing up whether to increase the business rates multiplier it charges businesses in the Square Mile, but a member of its finance committee has warned that this would amount to “spreadsheet” thinking.
While business rates are set nationally and usually absorbed into central government tax receipts, the City of London charges an additional multiplier – known as the City Premium – to cover local services like the City police force.
The local authority held an emergency finance meeting last week to discuss how to plug an unexpected shortfall in central government funding and is weighing up a hike to this multiplier to generate more income, as first reported by the Financial Times.
Stephen Hodgson, a City councillor and a member of the finance committee, has urged the local authority to resist further hikes to the business rates multiplier, warning that a higher tax burden could undermine the finance hub’s global reputation.
He told City AM: “It’s a big political decision. It’s not a spreadsheet decision, and I think it’s [being] interpreted as a decision about plugging a gap on a spreadsheet. And actually, it should be about attractiveness, competitiveness, [and] economic growth.”
The City Premium was first introduced in 1990, and the finance committee member said that recent hikes to the premium mean that “there is a noticeable gap between the level in the Square Mile versus anywhere else”.
For the 2026/27 financial year, the City set an additional 3.2p business rates multiplier, up from 0.8p in the 2020/21 financial year. In the last financial year, the City raised £45.7m from its business rates premium.
Hodgson said the mood in the local authority is leaning towards further hikes: “There’s very much a discussion along the lines of ‘we’ve got this gap, let’s just put business rates premiums up’”.
But he said he is attempting to lobby the City against a “spreadsheet” approach. “This is a matter of strategic importance in terms of competitiveness, [because] businesses respond to higher costs.”
City faces Budget tax raid
Hodgson pointed towards looming Budget tax raids – including the bank surcharge and government-set business rates multipliers for office buildings – which are set to hit the City hard.
“When we do have control of something, and it’s entirely in our control, such as business rates premiums, we need to be on the side of businesses,” he said.
Tax revenue raised by the City of London Corporation is used to cover services for its 9,000 residents – like council housing and adult social care – as well as the City of London Police, which focuses on fraud and economic crime.
The future of the Square Mile’s police force is hanging in the balance. An upcoming Home Office review is weighing up whether to scrap the force, by rolling it into the Metropolitan Police.
The abolition of the City of London Police, while unwanted by many in the Square Mile, would weaken the case for higher business rates multipliers because the City would not have to cover its budget, Hodgson claimed.
A spokesperson for the City of London Corporation said its members are “considering a range of options as part of the budget-setting process” and will set out its five-year financial plan in March next year.
They added: “The City of London Corporation provides high-quality public services that workers, residents, visitors, and students expect of a global financial district.
“This matters, as the Square Mile is home to the UK’s financial and professional services sector, which generates 12 per cent of all tax receipts and helps pay for vital public services delivered across the UK.”

items.title: B&M joins battle to ‘cherry pick’ Poundland stores in sale
items.summary: Discount retailer B&M has joined the tussle to pick off select Poundland stores as its Boston-based owner Gordon Brothers eyes a rushed sale of the company. London-listed B&M European Value Retail is interested in acquiring a small number of Poundland stores, should the retailer be broken up if a buyer for the whole company is [...]
items.body:
B&M joins battle to ‘cherry pick’ Poundland stores in sale
Discount retailer B&M has joined the tussle to pick off select Poundland stores as its Boston-based owner Gordon Brothers eyes a rushed sale of the company.
London-listed B&M European Value Retail is interested in acquiring a small number of Poundland stores, should the retailer be broken up if a buyer for the whole company is not found, sources told City AM.
B&M will face competition from budget supermarket Lidl for Poundland’s best-placed stores. Last week, City AM revealed the German grocer had bid for a single Poundland shop in the hopes of ‘cherry picking’ a handful more in the event of a break-up.
A number of other retailers are understood to be interested in acquiring some of Poundland’s stores. These include The Range and Poundstretcher, which is owned by Fortress Investment Group.
Lidl’s rival Aldi and B&M competitor Home Bargains were reported to have been sniffing around the sale but City AM understands neither have submitted a formal bid.
Beyond the retailers hoping to snap up extra sites from Poundland’s sale, a number of investment groups have submitted bids for the business.
Poundland’s management has expressed preference for the offer tabled by Martin Property Group, the Irish firm which recently bought National Car Parks (NCP).
Revamped board weighs up bids
B&M’s interest in Poundland, first reported by Sky News, comes after Gordon Brothers parachuted in three M&A experts to join Poundland managing director Barry Williams and finance chief Shaun Wills.
Andrew Kirkpatrick, Stephen Welch and Dominic Young have begun reviewing the bids tabled for the retailer, in the hopes of securing a sale before the crucial pre-Christmas trading period kicks off in earnest.
The three restructuring experts were added to Poundland’s board to ease concerns expressed by Martin Property Group’s rival bidders that they would not stand a chance against a bidder who had been publicly endorsed by the company’s management.
Gordon Brothers kicked off its sale of Poundland last month, little more than a year after buying the company for a nominal £1 fee from retail group PepCo.
A spokesperson for Gordon Brothers said last week: “After commencing a thorough sale process for the entirety of the company, prompted by interest from several parties, active discussions continue with a number of potential acquirers.
“The offers include those from buyers for the whole business and also indicative offers for significant viable parts of the business from established retail operators.”

items.body:
FREEE is expanding its breakfast cereal range with the launch of Mixed Berry Flakes (325g, RRP £4.15), a crunchy flake cereal packed with delicious, freeze-dried strawberries, cherries and blueberries.
Listed online at freee-foods.co.uk and with Ocado from w/c 19th October, the new cereal gives gluten free shoppers access to the popular flake and red berry fruit combination, without compromising on taste or texture.
Made in FREEE’s own facilities in the UK, Mixed Berry Flakes combines crunchy cereal flakes made from brown rice and maize, with a generous mix of freeze-dried berries, delivering a delicious burst of fruity flavour and satisfying crunch.
It is high in fibre and low in fat, contains no artificial colours, flavours or preservatives, and is made without any of the top 14 allergens, making it suitable for many dietary choices. The cereal is also certified gluten free by Coeliac UK.
Clare Marriage, FREEE founder, said: “Ensuring there are delicious gluten free versions of shoppers’ favourite foods is a key motivation for us. FREEE Mixed Berry Flakes brings the winning combination of crunchy flakes and berries to the free-from aisle with the reassurance of FREEE’s gluten free credentials.
We’ve been really pleased with the reaction to the cereal. The combination of crunchy flakes and delicious freeze-dried berries makes it a great breakfast, whether you’re looking for something free-from or not. We’re excited to give our existing shoppers another cereal to choose from and bring more variety to the gluten free breakfast category.”
Mixed Berry Flakes will be available from w/c 19th October at Ocado and freee-foods.co.uk, RSP £4.15 for 325g.

items.body:
The wait is over: the new Kissabel® season in the Northern Hemisphere has just begun. The innovative range of coloured-flesh apples – from pink to deep red – returns to the market with excellent prospects and a series of activities designed to support retailers and engage consumers. The commercial window opened in early September in the first markets of the Northern Hemisphere, continuing with different and specific timings depending on each country, with the aim, in some cases, of running until January.
Once again, IFORED programme partners will take centre stage: US-based Next Big Thing (NBT), British Worldwide Fruit, and French partners Mylord-Gerfruit, Mesfruits and Blue Whale. They will be followed by Italian partners, the NovaMela Consortium (Melinda, VIP, Rivoira, La Trentina and VOG), Germany’s Red Apple Germany (Elbe-Obst, Obst vom Bodensee) and Switzerland’s Fenaco, all focusing solely on the Rouge variety.
With its inimitable appearance, exceptional taste and distinctive identity, Kissabel® is once again set to win over a young, curious audience drawn to surprising, naturally flavoursome products.
The new season opens with a major change in the leadership of the project: Jeremy Linsell takes on the role of Programme Manager for Kissabel®, taking the baton, in a spirit of continuity, from Emmanuel de Lapparent, who has led the brand’s development since its earliest days. A graduate in Agricultural Engineering, Linsell brings more than 27 years of experience at the highest levels of the fresh fruit industry, including over twenty years as a grower and more than eight years dedicated to technical and strategic consultancy for the development and management of new varieties. He has held key roles at leading organisations and global varietal innovation programmes. Since 2017, he has also been a member of the Technical Committee of the IFORED Programme, where he has been personally involved in evaluating varietal selections, international-scale testing and commercial development, culminating in the introduction of the first red-fleshed apple to the British market.
“I am delighted to take the helm of Kissabel® and to guide the brand through its next phase of development,” said Jeremy Linsell. “I firmly believe in the unique value of this apple, capable of surprising consumers and bringing genuine innovation to the fresh produce aisle. The project is built on the strength and expertise of leading international partners. By working together, I am confident we will fully unlock the extraordinary potential and disruptive spirit of Kissabel®.”
Meanwhile, de Lapparent continues involvement taking on the role of IFORED president alongside becoming director general of Dalival.
United Kingdom: building momentum and looking to the future
In the UK, partner Worldwide Fruit will launch the season in late September, with a sales window running through to December. All three varieties in the range – Rouge, Jaune and Orange – will be available on the market, backed by promotional activities in support of the brand, both in-store and across digital channels.
“The response to last season’s campaign was extremely positive, and for this new season we want to build on and relaunch that success,” says Hannah McIlfatrick, commercial director at Worldwide Fruit. “We remain firmly committed to the Kissabel® project and continue to invest in its development, which we believe can bring value to the whole category. Our aim is to gradually extend the commercial window, supporting this growth with a planting programme for the Rouge and Jaune varieties running through to 2030.”
United States: Kissabel® set to delight consumers
In the United States, North American partner Next Big Thing (NBT) plans to launch the season between mid- and late September, reaching peak sales in October and wrapping up the campaign in November. The Rouge and Jaune varieties will be available.
“This year, we will be working closely with our retail partners on new communication materials designed to link Kissabel® to the seasonal themes of autumn and Halloween,” says Brianna Shales, marketing director at Stemilt Growers and Next Big Thing (NBT) spokesperson for the Kissabel® project. “Through engaging campaign taglines such as ‘Dare to Try’ and ‘Autumn Outside, Unexpected Inside’, we will invite shoppers to discover the surprise inside the fruit. In addition, the wide range of pack formats will help retailers create high-impact displays and encourage consumers to try the product.”
France: domestic market and strategic exports
In France, the campaign started in early September and will continue until November. Partners Mylord-Gerfruit, Mesfruits and Blue Whale will be marketing the range, with a primary focus on the Jaune variety, supported by select volumes of the Rouge variety.
“Kissabel® has very interesting potential because it combines strong visual distinctiveness with an equally distinctive taste experience,” comments Marion Dufossé, international brands development manager at Blue Whale. “We are therefore continuing to develop the brand’s presence, not only in the French market but also in Asia and the Middle East, through targeted activities with our partners and customers.”
Germany: focus on the surprise effect of the flesh
In Germany, the Kissabel® season – focused exclusively on the Rouge variety – will, as is now traditional, launch at Halloween and run through to Christmas. This year, partner Red Apple Germany (Elbe-Obst, Obst vom Bodensee) has developed a communication plan designed to highlight the product’s most distinctive feature: its red flesh. Among the initiatives planned, two key campaigns stand out: the Kissabel® Surprise social media challenge, which will invite users to share videos of their reaction to their first bite, and the Red Creations by Kissabel® platform, designed to guide consumers – including in-store – towards creative recipes and festive baking ideas featuring Kissabel®.
“Kissabel® offers extraordinary engagement power precisely thanks to the ‘surprise factor’ of its red flesh,” explains Jens Anderson, marketing manager for Kissabel® at Red Apple Germany. “By combining digital activities with initiatives in supermarkets, our aim is to showcase the spectacular nature of this fruit, supporting our retail partners and surprising consumers.”
Italy: Kissabel® Rouge takes centre stage in November and December
In Italy, the campaign run by the NovaMela Consortium (Melinda, VIP, Rivoira, La Trentina and VOG) will get into full swing during November and December, focusing entirely on the Rouge variety. The main objective will be to ensure a strong, consistent brand presence in both wholesale markets and with retailers, further supported by promotional and communication initiatives developed by the individual member businesses.
“We are looking very confidently ahead to the new Kissabel® season. Harvest forecasts point to positive quality and quantity standards, which lead us to expect a good pack-out rate,” comments Andrea Fedrizzi, marketing director at Melinda and NovaMela spokesperson. “Kissabel® continues to offer consumers a unique experience, thanks to the visual impact of its red flesh, its distinctive taste and its premium positioning. We firmly believe in the brand’s long-term prospects and are ready to bring even greater awareness to this extraordinary apple, working together with all the partners.”
Switzerland: a dynamic campaign for Halloween
In Switzerland, partner Fenaco will launch the Rouge variety season by capitalising on the Halloween period. The campaign will be defined by a high sales tempo, driven by a substantial programme of promotional activities, with the aim of maximising volumes and completing distribution by the end of the year.
The place to experience the excellence of the range first-hand is Fruit Attraction (Madrid, 6–8 October), at Stand A16 in Hall 8: an unmissable opportunity to be immersed in the world of Kissabel® and be impressed by its incredible colours and extraordinary taste.

items.body:
Tom Parker Creamery is expanding its growing portfolio of added-value whole milks with the launch of Golden Milk, a new gently spiced whole milk drink made with turmeric, cinnamon, honey and black pepper.
Developed for those seeking out natural products to support holistic health and wellness, Golden Milk features turmeric, which contains curcumin, a naturally occurring plant compound known to help reduce inflammation and support healthy liver function.  Turmeric is paired with warming cinnamon, a spice associated with aiding digestion and a healthy metabolism.
Believed to be a UK category first the 500ml ready-to-drink Golden Milk will launch into Waitrose and Ocado from 21 October, joining Tom Parker Creamery’s Vitamin-Enriched Whole Milk and Bedtime Milk as the Somerset creamery continues to carve out a distinctive position in added-value and functional dairy drinks.
Made with free-range British whole milk, Golden Milk takes inspiration from the traditional turmeric-based Indian drink haldi doodh – literally “turmeric milk” – which combines warm milk with turmeric and has long been enjoyed in South Asia. Golden milk has grown in popularity driven by increasing consumer interest in natural ingredients, botanicals and food and drink associated with health and wellbeing.
The launch builds on a wider consumer shift towards whole foods, recognisable ingredients and minimally processed products – trends that Tom Parker Creamery has increasingly placed at the heart of its proposition. Its existing added-value milk portfolio includes Vitamin-Enriched Whole Milk and Bedtime Milk, with the creamery positioning added-value dairy as an opportunity to bring new usage occasions and innovation to shake up the milk fixture.
Rob Yates, CEO of Tom Parker Creamery, said: “Consumers are increasingly looking for more from everyday food and drink, but at the same time they want products made with natural ingredients they recognise. We think dairy is brilliantly placed to respond to both trends.
“Golden Milk brings together our free-range British whole milk with turmeric, cinnamon, honey and black pepper to create something that supports wellbeing as part of a healthy lifestyle. It’s a simple, delicious drink that can be enjoyed chilled straight from the fridge or gently warmed, opening up another occasion for whole milk beyond the traditional breakfast table.”
Golden Milk follows the successful development of Tom Parker Creamery’s added-value milk range, including its Vitamin-Enriched Whole Milk and Bedtime Milk, launched in 2025. The latter helped establish the brand in functional dairy, combining whole milk with botanicals and tapping into growing consumer interest in food and drink that fits into wider wellbeing routines. Tom Parker Creamery has previously identified “adding value to the milk category” and developing milks enriched with natural ingredients as an important part of its evolving brand proposition.
The new product retains the hallmarks of the wider Tom Parker Creamery range, including British whole milk and the brand’s distinctive glass bottle packaging with recyclable paper labels.

items.body:
Irish artisan chocolate brand Grá Chocolates by award-winning chocolatier Gráinne Mullins has unveiled its 2026 festive collection: a hand-painted, hand-crafted line-up spanning Christmas trees, hampers, hot chocolate bombs and an advent calendar, all made in County Galway using the finest ingredients. From its luxury advent calendar to a whiskey-and-coffee-inspired Christmas Cracker chocolate, the range is built for gifting, sharing and seasonal indulgence.
GRÁ FESTIVE RANGE 2026
Christmas Selection Box: £49.00 / 180g
12 hand-painted crescent chocolates in festive flavours including: Winter Wonderland (white chocolate, cranberry, star anise), Gingerbread House (ginger, cinnamon, blonde chocolate), Christmas Cracker (whiskey caramel, coffee ganache) and Under The Mistletoe (spiced orange, dark chocolate).
Hot Chocolate Bomb Range: £15.00 / 1 piece
Hand-painted bronze chocolate bombs filled with real chocolate chunks – melt into a mug of warm milk for an indulgent hot chocolate.
Chocolate Christmas Trees: £18.00 / 100g
A collection of six flavours: Orange Festive Feast (milk chocolate, candied orange), Milk and Cookies, Hazelnut and Almond (dark chocolate, Achill Island sea salt), Pistachio and Raspberry (white chocolate), Ginger All The Way (blonde chocolate) and Mint Snowball (white chocolate, peppermint).
Chocolate Christmas Trees: £18.00 / 100g
A collection of six flavours: Orange Festive Feast (milk chocolate, candied orange), Milk and Cookies, Hazelnut and Almond (dark chocolate, Achill Island sea salt), Pistachio and Raspberry (white chocolate), Ginger All The Way (blonde chocolate) and Mint Snowball (white chocolate, peppermint).
Luxury Christmas Crackers: £9.00 / 18g (available individually or as a box of five)
Signature Lil Bit Salty chocolate crackers, each with a festive paper hat and a joke inside – designed by an Irish designer.
Advent Calendar: £100.00 / 290g
A daily countdown of indulgent chocolates, including Lil’ Bit Salty and Gingerbread House flavours.
Advent calendars are available to pre order now.
Mince Pie Heart: £49.00 / 1 piece
A large milk chocolate heart with a brandy butter and mince pie-inspired ganache, dried fruit and blonde chocolate shortcrust base
Twinkling Lights Collection: £30.00 / 80g (10-piece) or £49.00 / 160g (20-piece)
An all-new seasonal selection of hand-painted chocolates inspired by the warmth and nostalgia of an Irish Christmas.
Seasonal Hot Chocolate – £24.00 / 300g
Available to purchase from Tuesday 1st September
Gingerbread Hot Chocolate (milk and white chocolate, fresh ginger) and Pumpkin Spice Hot Chocolate (caramel-white chocolate, cinnamon, pumpkin) – both high in cacao content.
Christmas Hampers: Bespoke pricing
A range of hamper sizes available on request, tailored to suit.
